The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and searchlight MVPA results (voxelwise analyses, cluster-corrected) and provide Talairach coordinates and figures. Contrasts compare decision conditions (parametric uncertainty modulation; difficult>easy/low coherence>high coherence-type effects) and include a task versus active control (categorization vs letter-identification) analysis. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a well-established risky decision-making paradigm (experimental gamble vs control gamble) with contrasts of interest (experimental>control; high vs low probability; high vs low gain) and separate decision and outcome phases. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME for within-group effects and OLS for between-group effects) with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants include substance-using and control groups. Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for risky decision-making and meets the meta-analysis requirements for risky-DM contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, tables, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI (I4) while human subjects performed a risky decision-making task (choices between risky gambles and certain outcomes), it includes within-task contrasts comparing gamble versus certainty decisions (I5), reports group-level whole-brain searchlight MVPA maps with a group one-sample t-test and cluster correction (I6), uses an eligible participant sample (healthy adults) (I7), and presents whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), it is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is an empirical fMRI task study. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study tests decision-making processes (probabilistic and risk mechanisms) during pronoun reference resolution, directly manipulating uncertainty and risk. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 second-level random-effects) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Undetermined > Directly Determined; Indirectly Determined > Directly Determined) and a parametric uncertainty analysis (high > low uncertainty). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported with whole-brain coordinates and corrected thresholds. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making, includes appropriate contrasts, provides whole-brain group maps, and involves an eligible participant group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., task>rest-only contrasts, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study meets inclusion for the meta-analysis because it used fMRI while human participants made mixed gambles that included a prospective risk manipulation (prospective risk mixed gambles), and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and parametric contrasts relating neural activation to prospective risk magnitude. Although the paper also examines effort-based choices (which would be excluded), the presence of a well-specified risky decision-making task with whole-brain analyses (parametric risk levels analogous to high-risk > low-risk) satisfies the review’s scope. Participants were healthy adults and results/maps are available and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating rule certainty vs uncertainty. It reports within-task contrasts (uncertain > certain and certain > uncertain) that map onto ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported (FEAT, cluster-thresholded maps, figures, and tabulated cluster descriptions), and whole-brain ROI/network analyses are also provided. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study collected fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and ROI coordinates (I6, I8). However, the reported whole-brain contrasts described in the full text are task>background and epoch>rest (instruction/stimulus/confidence > rest) and ROI-defining contrasts were task>background; the paper does not present a qualifying condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast of the form required for perceptual-DM (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control task). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/rest). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (categorization) task manipulating motion coherence (perceptual salience) and distance from a category boundary (categorical salience). The paper reports condition-vs-condition analyses including parametric contrasts (e.g., BOLD modulation with motion coherence: low coherence > high coherence) and ANOVA interactions, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (cluster-corrected) and ROI confirmation. Participants are healthy adults. The manuscript includes complete sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition/parametric contrasts comparing decision conditions), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, no task>rest-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study acquired while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (face vs car categorization with color discrimination control) with manipulated stimulus coherence. The design includes condition-wise manipulations (high vs low coherence and task type) that yield condition contrasts interpretable as perceptual difficulty (e.g., low coherence > high coherence) and task-vs-control comparisons. Analysis is whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise mixed-effects GLM with cluster correction; results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and region summaries. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI evidence.

The study reports human fMRI during an ambiguous/uncertain decision-making task (matching-pennies). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguity/uncertainty (e.g., feedback > no-feedback; uncertain > certain; high- vs low-load) and an event-related feedback vs no-feedback contrast. Analyses are group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported MNI coordinates/ROIs. Participants are healthy adults. Results are clearly reported in main text (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only ROI; not contrasts vs baseline only; not connectivity-only; empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study uses fMRI during a risky decision-making game (I4) and reports within-task contrasts comparing non-match (risky) vs match (safe) anticipation and outcome contrasts (I5). Participant sample (OCD patients and controls) is acceptable (I7) and results are described in text/figures (I8). However, the paper reports task activation results primarily via region-of-interest (ROI) extractions (amygdala and nucleus accumbens) using templates from a prior study rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required for inclusion (I6). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only task activation reporting without whole-brain task results). Because it does not provide the requisite group-level whole-brain task activation maps, it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky vs. safe selections (risky > safe), and also reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected significance (AlphaSim). One-sample t-tests for within-group task effects and between-group contrasts are presented and described in tables and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which adolescents performed a lottery choice (risk) decision-making task during BOLD acquisition. The authors modeled a parametric regressor of coefficient of variation (CV) of chosen gambles and report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE-corrected), showing greater right amygdala activation to higher-risk versus lower-risk choices (equivalent to a 'high-risk > low-risk' contrast). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. The task and reported contrasts meet the risky-DM specifications, whole-brain maps/coordinates are provided, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or baseline-only). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study tests decision-making during fMRI with economic games involving risk/ambiguity (assurance and chicken games) and reports fMRI contrasts (e.g., AG vs CG). However, the paper’s neuroimaging results are reported only as region-of-interest (ROI) analyses because their exploratory whole-brain analysis yielded no significant voxels ("No voxels survived FWE correction") and no whole-brain coordinate/map results are provided for the task contrasts. Therefore the study does not provide a usable group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map as required. Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision tasks), I5 (between-condition contrast AG vs CG), I7 (healthy human participants). Inclusion not met: I6 (no reported whole-brain group-level/voxelwise task activation map). Exclusion applied: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human youth performing a well-established risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning, reporting within-task contrasts (risky vs nonrisky; gain vs loss) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis scope (risky decision-making) and all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) paradigm and the reported analyses focus on parametric PE regressors rather than contrasts that match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making comparisons. Specifically, no contrasts of the form risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses were performed) and I8 (results reported with coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined for this meta-analysis) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts are presented). Exclusion criterion invoked: E5 (task does not fit the risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM categories required). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence), satisfying the review focus. It reports condition-vs-condition contrasts that map onto perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., low coherence/hard > high coherence/easy; parametric "inverse dependence on coherence" and explicit "low coherence > high coherence" effects). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinate tables and surface maps (Table 3, figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are human and healthy; results are reported in text, figures, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided, so fulltext is complete. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (face/house discrimination) meeting the review scope. It collected BOLD data while human subjects performed a perceptual decision task (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition comparisons (face vs house, analyses across noise/difficulty and RT bins), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-vs-decision or difficulty contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (repeated-measures ANOVA, voxelwise GLM) with reported peak coordinates and ROI maps, fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting formats (I8). Participant group (healthy young adults) is acceptable under participant criteria (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not only task>baseline (E3), not PET (E4), are perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), include whole-brain results (not E6), are not connectivity-only (not E7), and are empirical data (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in human healthy adults that explicitly manipulates and reports neural correlates of decision-making under uncertainty (relative and mean uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps (coordinates, FWE-corrected clusters) linking trial-by-trial relative uncertainty to BOLD in RLPFC and mean uncertainty to DLPFC/SPL. Analyses include parametric contrasts (high vs low uncertainty effects) and group contrasts (explorers vs nonexplorers), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast beyond implicit baseline. Methods, results, and coordinates are reported in the main text (with supplemental materials available), and the task involves ambiguous/uncertain decision-making (uncertainty-driven exploration), which fits the meta-analysis’ ambiguous-DM domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-eligible task) are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment with human participants performing a sequential risk-taking task (opening boxes with a hidden ‘devil’) during scanning, satisfying I4. It provides within-task contrasts comparing outcome conditions relevant to risky decision-making (Optimum, Miss, Devil) and interaction/parametric contrasts tied to decision-related states (regret vs. relief), meeting I5. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (tables and figures), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adult humans, so I7 is satisfied. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (contrasts are condition-vs-condition, not task>rest only; whole-brain analyses reported; not PET; task is risky decision-making). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (delayed match-to-category) task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (searchlight) voxelwise statistical maps (t tests on cross-decoding accuracy with TFCE correction) that compare decision-related conditions (category discriminations across modalities), which constitute condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision making. The participant sample is healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM task), I5 (condition-vs-condition decision contrasts via decoding maps), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study (group, n=13) that administered a decision-making task under uncertainty (maze goal-search with partially observable states) and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (subtraction goal-search > visuomotor and parametric regressions with HCP entropy and BT probability). The task manipulates uncertainty/ambiguity about current state (HCP entropy), matching the meta-analysis’ ambiguous decision-making domain. Active control (yoked visuomotor) and within-task contrasts/regressors were used rather than implicit baseline. Methods state whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses with thresholding and reported coordinates. Participants were healthy humans. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that explicitly investigates risky decision-making. The task required choices between high-risk (40% chance $2.50) and low-risk (80% chance $1.25) gambles, and the authors report a direct contrast of high-risk > low-risk. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (one-sample t tests) with reported peak coordinates (Table 1) and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures/tables and the paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not task>baseline only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a perceptual/predictive-inference decision task manipulating uncertainty (high vs low noise) and surprise. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts (CPP, RU, reward) and pairwise contrasts (e.g., CPP>RU), perform whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses with appropriate correction, and present conjunction and contrast maps. These analyses constitute condition-vs-condition and parametric decision-making contrasts rather than task>baseline. The task maps onto perceptual decision-making (noise/coherence-like manipulation) and meets the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, includes whole-brain task activations, not only connectivity, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reason: This study conducted fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (meets I4) in human participants (adolescents and adults; meets I7). However, the imaging results are reported only as ROI-based analyses (ACC, VS, vmPFC) and discrete-state summaries, with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables presented; thus it qualifies as an ROI-only study (meets exclusion E6). In addition, the reported contrasts are feedback/decision condition comparisons (PFB, NFB-Stay, NFB-Switch) rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy), so it does not provide the required decision-making contrast form for the meta-analysis (fails I5 and I6). Therefore exclude under E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6.

This study collected fMRI data while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles), with within-subject contrasts between decision contexts (threat vs safe) and parametric modulation by expected subjective value. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and coordinates are reported; exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected results and ROI results are provided. Participants were healthy adults. Thus the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked maps comparing decision-making conditions (within-task contrasts), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making fMRI studies. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required (Exclusion E5). The tasks are value-based/affective decisions about pleasantness of thermal and olfactory stimuli (reward-based choice) rather than risky/uncertain or perceptual-coherence decisions targeted by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task condition contrast: easy vs difficult), I6 (group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task category — not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky financial decision-making task (lottery vs sure win) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (MESSAGE vs NO MESSAGE; ignore vs follow expert) and parametric whole-brain correlations with probability-weighted lottery value and sure-win magnitude, satisfying the requirement for decision-making contrasts. Whole-brain random-effects t-tests and thresholded statistical maps/activation coordinates are reported. The task involves risk (explicit probabilities), not rest-baseline-only contrasts, and is not PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a tactile perceptual decision-making task (spatial pattern discrimination) with parametric manipulation of difficulty. The authors modelled difficulty-related effects using parametric modulators derived from RTs (analogous to 'hard > easy' contrasts) and report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). They additionally provide MVPA results and full methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults. The design, analyses, and reported whole-brain activation maps satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task-vs-baseline only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Instead, one of the tasks is a delay discounting task (intertemporal choice), which is explicitly excluded (E5). Although the study includes whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I6), reports results in the main text (I8), and uses an eligible participant group (healthy adults; I7), it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for task type (I4) nor the decision-making-contrast requirement for the allowed DM domains (I5). Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study where adolescent girls performed a risky decision-making task (modified Jackpot) during scanning, with task contrasts comparing decision conditions (Play > Pass, LR > HR, Gain > Loss). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters), and results are described in the main text and supplements. The task qualifies as risky decision-making and multiple condition-versus-condition contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI results, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) decision-making task with monetary feedback and modeled three feedback conditions (win, lose-stay, lose-shift) at first level and a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis at second level. The authors report whole-brain group results for the lose-shift condition (FWE-corrected maps, clusters) and gPPI connectivity as supplementary analysis. The task involves uncertainty/probabilistic feedback (decision-making under uncertainty) and provides within-task condition contrasts (feedback conditions) qualifying under the review definitions. Participant groups are acceptable and results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps in the text/figures/SI. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of state-based dynamic reward learning (state-maximizing vs reward-maximizing choices) comparing younger and older adults. However, the task is a history-dependent reward-learning paradigm and does not manipulate or contrast risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or perceptual difficulty conditions as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The paper does meet some inclusion requirements: it reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (I6); uses healthy human participants (I7); and presents whole-brain results described in the text/figures (I8). It does not meet I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (it does not report the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Therefore it should be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents using the HiLo decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (pure uncertainty 50% vs probabilistic conditions). The primary contrast of interest is a condition-vs-condition contrast (50% condition vs other task conditions), which corresponds to an ambiguous/high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty comparison. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction are reported and thresholded maps/clusters are provided in tables and figures. The task and contrasts directly address ambiguous decision-making and meet the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans that includes a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) and a rule-based decision task, collected during whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports condition-versus-control contrasts (task trials vs control trials; manipulations of difficulty/coherence and regressions on uncertainty levels), provides whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding, and reports coordinates/activation patterns. Participants are healthy human adults. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (task > control and difficulty/coherence/uncertainty contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, not only ROI/connectivity, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a human fMRI study that manipulated risky and ambiguous gambles and tested neural correlates of belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation. The task clearly involves risk and ambiguity (Ellsberg-style urn gambles), and fMRI data were analyzed with whole-brain, group-level GLMs producing voxelwise statistical maps (parametric modulators for belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation) with cluster-level FWE correction. The study reports within-task contrasts/parametric effects (e.g., value updating, belief updating adjusted for expectancy violation), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Participants were healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore this empirical fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study (3T) in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating uncertainty and financial incentive. It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to the review (e.g., High vs Low uncertainty, Financial_High vs Neutral_High) matching ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM8 results with tables of peaks, figures, and cluster thresholds; small-volume corrections are also reported but whole-brain contrasts are present. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a delayed matching-to-sample (perceptual) decision-making task (checking task) during scanning. It includes at least one within-task decision-making contrast (decision-making followed by checking behavior (DFCB+) > decision-making not followed by checking behavior (DFCB−)), reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects, FDR-corrected). Participant groups (OCD patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging acquisition, preprocessing and statistics), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a predictive-inference decision task in the scanner (subjects placed a bucket to infer a hidden helicopter location under uncertainty). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (searchlight RSA and group t-maps, cluster correction) linking neural patterns to model-derived decision variables (relative uncertainty, change-point probability, learning rate) — i.e., within-task comparisons and parametric effects akin to high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty. Results are reported as whole-brain maps/figures and tables. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies fMRI during a decision task under uncertainty (I4), contains within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons of decision variables (I5), provides whole-brain group-level maps (I6), participants are an acceptable group (I7), and whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is excluded because it does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps; analyses are ROI-based only. (a) Exclusion met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (contrast of ambiguous task vs control condition / within-task comparisons), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). (c) Inclusion not met: I6 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because failing I6 triggers exclusion under E6, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a sequential foraging task with probabilistic (risky) outcomes. It meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with probabilistic/risky choices), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric effects comparing foraging vs waiting and value differences between choice options), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported with FWE correction and maps available), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables; supplementary data shared). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and contains within-task contrasts rather than only between-group effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full manuscript reports an fMRI study where human participants performed a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (Card-Deck). The paper includes within-group and between-group voxelwise contrasts (decision under risk vs decision under ambiguity; bet vs safe), with group-level whole-brain analyses and tables of activation coordinates. The task and contrasts match risky and ambiguous DM definitions in the meta-analysis. Whole-brain, group-level activation maps are reported (voxelwise GLM, thresholds and cluster correction described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that administered a perceptual decision-making task (visual motion direction discrimination) during task fMRI and reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps. The authors modelled parametric effects of motion coherence (20/40/80%) across trials, providing within-task contrasts equivalent to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low-coherence/hard vs high-coherence/easy via parametric modulation). Task-related whole-brain group analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps) and peak coordinates are reported. Participants are healthy humans. Although the paper emphasizes resting-state connectivity, the presence of whole-brain task activation maps and appropriate within-task contrasts meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

Although this is an fMRI study (Stoplight Task) of risky decision-making with whole-brain, group-level analyses, it does not report an explicit decision-making contrast of the required form (e.g., risky > safe or task > active control). The paper reports go and stop trials modeled versus implicit baseline and compares social-context conditions (mother vs adult) for those trial types, but no risky>safe (or equivalent) contrast is presented. Thus the study’s only decision-related contrasts appear to be against implicit baseline, which meets exclusion criterion E3.

This is an fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (modified cups task) performed by human participants (I4). The paper reports relevant within-task contrasts (risky > sure / risky–sure and related target×situation×choice contrasts) that match the admissible risky-DM contrasts (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results reported with whole-brain FWE correction and coordinate information (I6, I8). Participants are healthy young adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-task contrasts vs rest, or non-decision tasks) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (tactile grating orientation) with simultaneous confidence ratings. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (cluster-level FWE correction) and provides contrasts that qualify (perceptual task > motor-control trials, easy vs difficult, correct vs incorrect, and parametric modulation by confidence). Results are presented as figures and tables. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (perceptual task > control and difficulty contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed a risky decision-making task (risky-gains). The paper reports a within-task contrast comparing risky > safe choices (GLT risky vs safe) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (linear mixed effects and robust regressions) with cluster-corrected results and region descriptions. Participants include HIV+ and seronegative controls (acceptable per criteria). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only, and includes within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making (rapid evidence accumulation/Go–No-Go ‘‘baseball’’) task. The paper reports voxelwise GLM parameter estimates and whole-brain searchlight AUC/p-value maps and conducts within-task contrasts between decision conditions (Correct Go vs Correct No-Go; Correct No-Go vs Incorrect No-Go, etc.), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making contrast. Participants (n=11) are humans and whole-brain task-evoked maps are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) during scanning (I4 satisfied) and reports a task>control contrast (IGT > non-gambling control) (I5 satisfied). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses were restricted to an anatomically defined VMPFC region (ROI-based analyses); the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or unmasked whole-brain results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Hence EXCLUDED due to E6.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic object-reversal decision-making task (pORT) with explicit uncertainty/probabilistic outcomes. The authors report group-level, voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (used to identify ventral striatal voxels at P<0.001 uncorrected and report coordinates x=12,y=16,z=-5) and then parametric contrasts comparing decision-making conditions ("learned" vs "not yet learned") and modulation by uncertainty (inverted U-shaped response with maximal activation at ~50% learning). These constitute within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision making. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate reporting are present (and used to define ROI), and participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g. PET, only ROI/no whole-brain, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus non-risk (mean color pump > mean white pump), parametric (linear color > linear white) contrasts of risk level, and outcome contrasts (Explosions > Cashouts), all analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. Participants (heavy drinkers) are an acceptable group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task, with task versus active control block contrasts (experimental block vs control block). Group-level whole-brain one-sample and two-sample t-tests were performed and reported, and results are described in text, tables and figures. Participants were healthy adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI task contrasts and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This study meets the meta-analysis criteria: (1) It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making (Gabor detection) task (I4). (2) It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., expectation-incongruent > expectation-congruent; unexpected > expected), satisfying the required decision-making condition contrasts for perceptual DM (I5). (3) Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates (I6). (4) Participant sample consists of healthy adult humans (I7). (5) Whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures (I8). The full text supplied includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Given these points, the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This study is excluded because its decision-making task does not match the meta-analysis focus (Exclusion E5). The paper investigates offline replay and revaluation in a multi-step RL/planning paradigm rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making per the meta-analysis definitions. Although the task includes noisy rewards (uncertainty) and contrasts between revaluation and control conditions, it does not implement canonical risk (e.g., risky > safe) or ambiguity (high uncertainty > low uncertainty) or perceptual difficulty contrasts (hard > easy) required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (human participant sample within acceptable populations), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (did not conduct fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined), I5 (does not present one of the admitted decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (n=8) that directly tests decision making under uncertainty (probabilistic reasoning tasks: balls-in-a-bottle and personality survey). It reports a condition-vs-condition contrast comparing decision making under uncertainty to decision making under certainty (ambiguous > non-ambiguous), using whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses with corrected voxelwise statistics and tables/figures of coordinates. Participants are healthy; results are reported in figures and a coordinate table. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of ambiguous decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with an active control task (arrows). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dANOVA3, cluster-corrected maps) and provide cluster tables/coordinates. The key contrast (dots task > arrows control) and ramp-vs-down-ramp interaction test perceptual evidence accumulation (perceptual task > control task and task-related ramping). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a categorization task that includes ambiguous decision trials (inverse base rate effect). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., comparisons of activation on ambiguous trials depending on response type and model-based parametric modulators for similarity vs. dissimilarity evidence) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected) with tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults and full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria are met (no PET, no ROI-only, not task>rest only). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI (I4), contains relevant within-task contrasts (I5), reports group whole-brain maps (I6), involves an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures/tables consistent with acceptable reporting (I8).

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=5) of perceptual decision making using a dot-motion/color coherence task. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses testing parametric contrasts of coherence (i.e., low vs high coherence / hard > easy comparisons) and presents statistical maps, tables, and ROI analyses. The task and contrasts directly match perceptual decision-making criteria (parameterized motion/color coherence; attended vs ignored conditions). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion (introduction, materials and methods, results, modeling, connectivity, discussion), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (this is not PET; contrasts are condition-vs-condition parametric, not only baseline; whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion for meta-analysis of fMRI perceptual decision-making.

Excluded per E5: The task is a reinforcement-learning probabilistic reward/loss learning paradigm focused on prediction error signals, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported with FWE-corrected results), I7 (participant group qualifies: schizophrenia patients and controls), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in the text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the task does not constitute one of the review’s target decision-making domains—risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM—as operationalized), and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast of the admitted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; contrasts center on prediction-error regressors and gain>loss motivational context rather than the specified risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a decision-making task that involves uncertainty about outcomes and feedback during learning. It includes within-task contrasts comparing high-uncertainty (exploratory) versus low-uncertainty (proficiency) phases and contrasts of gains vs. losses and correct vs. wrong feedback, i.e. condition-versus-condition comparisons relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM2) voxelwise analyses are reported with coordinates and cluster results. Participants are healthy adult females. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, coordinates) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET only, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight) performed in the scanner, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts including Go > Stop (risky > safe) and other relevant contrasts (Crash > NoCrash), meeting I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds (tables and figures), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample (healthy adolescents) is an eligible group under I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not only task>implicit baseline), results include whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), and this is not PET or non-empirical. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This study reports fMRI of human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) with within-task contrasts (risky vs safe) and reports voxel-wise group-level analyses and coordinates. The methods describe voxel-wise analyses and supplemental whole-brain activation patterns; results include risky > safe comparisons and within-group relationships. Participants include substance users and controls. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI, task-contrast, group-level voxelwise reporting, participant, and reporting-forms criteria.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for decision-making contrasts. Exclusion: E3 applies — the critical task contrast reported is 'last reversal error compared to implicit (unmodeled) baseline' (task > implicit baseline), and the study does not present condition-versus-condition contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinates are reported), I7 (participants are human healthy subjects, an allowable group), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is a probabilistic reversal learning/set-shifting task and is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review), and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude on the basis of E3 (only implicit-baseline contrasts).

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in 9–11 year-old humans performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). It includes within-task contrasts comparing Decision versus Directed (control) trials (e.g., risky Decision > Directed sham trials), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM with nonparametric permutation testing) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Participant characteristics fall within eligible age groups. Results are reported in the main text and tables (whole-brain coordinates/clusters), satisfying the meta-analysis’ reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a 4-arm bandit decision-making task involving uncertainty (reward probabilities, reversals). The authors report whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (GLMs) and thresholded statistical maps (with multiple-comparisons correction) and have uploaded maps to NeuroVault. Key contrasts/regressors include model entropy (changes in uncertainty/high vs low entropy) and exploitation vs exploration, which correspond to ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and within-task condition comparisons. Results are reported across the whole brain (figures, corrected maps, ROI/peak coordinates) and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Participants are healthy human volunteers. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, empirical fMRI data reported).

The study used simultaneous EEG-fMRI with human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (meets I4). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (meets I6) with acceptable participant sample (meets I7) and whole-brain results presented in text/tables (meets I8). However, it does not present at least one contrast that matches the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrasts (I5) — e.g., there is no reported ‘risky > safe’, ‘high-risk > low-risk’, ‘high uncertainty > low uncertainty’, or perceptual ‘hard > easy’ contrast during the decision phase. The reported contrasts/regressors are outcome-locked parametric regressors for prediction-error valence and surprise (EEG-informed and model-based), not the decision-condition contrasts required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study fails to satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) during scanning and included risk/ambiguity manipulations (easy, hard, ambiguous trials and shock anticipation linked to performance). The analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., coherence modulation, a 2×2 RepHigh/RepLow × Easy/Uncertain ANOVA, and parametric conformity/dissent contrasts), and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM8 second-level random-effects analyses; FDR and SVC corrections) with coordinates/tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and reports an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain analyses (I6), includes healthy human participants (I7), and reports whole-brain results in the text (I8). However, the task is a social feedback-based person-perception learning paradigm (predicting ‘yes’/‘no’ responses of others) and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The study’s contrasts (e.g., incorrect vs. correct feedback; parametric modulation by learning state; yea-sayer vs. naysayer) do not match the required risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Excluded on that basis.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic reversal learning (reward-guided) decision-making task with uncertain probabilistic outcomes. It reports within-task contrasts (exploratory vs exploitative trials; model-based prediction-error regressors PEDU/PESU) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates). The task involves probabilistic reward contingencies (80/20) and adaptive decision-making under uncertainty, fitting the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic two-armed bandit decision-making task (uncertain/risky reward learning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps) for a decision-related parametric contrast (chosen expected value Q at time of choice) and for outcome-related RPE regressors, satisfying the requirement for a within-task, decision-related contrast. Participants are healthy human adults (younger and older). Whole-brain results are presented with coordinates and figures. Although the study also collected PET, it is not a PET-only paper and includes unmasked, whole-brain fMRI activation maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in human participants (n=22) using a perceptual decision-making task (trajectory endpoint estimation) with parametrically manipulated stimulus noise/precision (hard vs easy perceptual conditions). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, cluster-corrected Z-maps) linking brain activity to trial-wise perceptual precision, statistical-model precision, accuracy, and disparity measures. These constitute within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of decision difficulty/precision akin to hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence) and thus meet the required decision-making contrast criterion. The manuscript contains full Methods, Results, and Discussion and clearly reports whole-brain activation maps and tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI data collected while participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task), includes condition contrasts such as risky > safe (choice phase) and other within-task contrasts, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANCOVA, whole-brain and ROI results, with clusterwise maps and coordinates), and includes eligible participant groups (ASD, OCD, and typically developing adolescents). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorizing happy vs angry faces with clear vs noisy images), fulfilling I4. It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (noisy > clear; hard > easy) relevant to perceptual DM, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses are reported (second-level t-tests with FDR correction and a table of activated regions), meeting I6 and I8. Participant characteristics are acceptable (healthy adults), satisfying I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7), and does not report only task>rest contrasts as the sole decision-related contrast (E3). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans where participants performed a risky decision-making task (skewed gambling) during scanning (I4). The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (skewed vs symmetric; positive vs negative skew) suitable as decision-making contrasts (I5). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, second-level regression analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participants are healthy adults (I7), and whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded task types). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans of risky decision making using mixed gambles and choices (P_max, G_max, L_min). The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., P_max > magnitude-sensitive choices; G_max vs L_min) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected maps). Participants are healthy young adults. Results include whole-brain activation maps and ROI/ connectivity analyses reported in text and supplemental materials. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making with whole-brain contrasts and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus riskless decisions (Mean Color > Mean White and Linear Color > Linear White), satisfying the required risky-DM contrast formats. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FSL FLAME, cluster correction) with coordinates/figures/tables and omnibus and pairwise results, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participant groups (adolescents, including substance users and controls) are acceptable per the eligibility rules. Results are presented in full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) with supplementary figures/tables; the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This full-text reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing risky decision-making (and intertemporal) tasks, with explicit within-task and between-condition contrasts (e.g., Risk > Control, Risk > Delay, Delay > Control, Delay > Risk, and choice-predictive contrasts). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (FLAME, thresholding reported) with coordinates and tables/figures provided. Participant sample (N=23 healthy adults) is within eligible populations. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that used a perceptual decision-making task (backward-masked majority function task) manipulating task difficulty/information rate (hard > easy) and exposure time. It reports within-subject condition contrasts (main effects of information entropy, reciprocal of ET, and their interaction) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

Only the abstract/full text excerpt is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract we can confirm fMRI was used during a decision-making task (I4) and participant type is acceptable (I7). However, the full text is not available to verify critical inclusion criteria: there is no clear description of the specific task contrasts meeting I5 (e.g., risky>safe or equivalent) nor confirmation that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps were reported (I6). It is also unclear whether results are reported beyond summary activations (tables/coordinates) as required (I8). Because the full text is incomplete and these mandatory inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article.

This is an fMRI study in which human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) in the scanner (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts involving decision types (go=risky and stop=safe) across social contexts (peer vs parent), i.e., comparisons of decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain random-effects maps with cluster correction and results shared on NeuroVault (meets I6 and I8). Participant sample falls within acceptable ages and groups (meets I7). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study does not rely solely on baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activation (not ROI-only), and includes task contrasts beyond seed-based connectivity (so E3,E4,E6,E7,E8,E9 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a limited-offer decision task that manipulates risk/uncertainty (accept vs wait with chance of losing the offer). The authors report group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain and ROI), including parametric contrasts for choice conflict (entropy/high vs low) and expected precision (state-dependent confidence), with reported whole-brain significant clusters and midbrain ROI peaks. These constitute within-task condition comparisons (e.g., high vs low conflict/precision) relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions via parametric modulators), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only baseline contrasts; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; empirical data). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study had human participants performing a tactile perceptual decision-making task (vibrotactile pattern discrimination) with manipulated decision difficulty (intact/partially/fully scrambled) and immediate vs delayed response conditions. The analysis included group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and parametric modulation by difficulty (i.e., hard > easy type contrasts), and reported task-related whole-brain activation (ROIs derived from corrected voxelwise results). Participants were healthy volunteers. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI with perceptual DM), I5 (decision-related contrasts/parametric difficulty modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not baseline-only contrasts; not ROI-only reporting; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential gambles with targets). The paper reports within-task, parametric contrasts (regressors for target level, expected value, variance/risk, skewness) and tests neural correlates of these decision variables at the group level using SPM; results are reported as voxelwise group analyses with stereotactic coordinates and thresholds (whole-brain results and small-volume corrections). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (I4), contains within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to risky decisions (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), uses an eligible participant sample (I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). The provided full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task fMRI in human participants performing a risky multi-step gambling decision-making task (Goal-Instructed Gambling task). It includes within-task condition contrasts that directly compare decision states (quota-severity and strategy-optimization contrasts, e.g., Imp>High>Low>Easy and Low/High>Non/Imp), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-size correction and peak coordinates (dlPFC, dACC, AI, dmPFC). Results include within-task contrasts and ROI/correlation follow-ups, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not only connectivity, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with trial-by-trial confidence measures. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates and statistical maps linking BOLD to parametric contrasts (e.g., confidence-related modulation, EEG-derived high vs. low confidence), satisfying within-task condition comparisons. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are not only task>rest). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

The paper reports an fMRI gambling decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (Win vs Lose blocks) in human participants, providing within-task contrasts (Lose vs Win) and a group-level repeated-measures GLM whole-brain analysis with coordinates and statistical maps. It thus meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (within-task contrast: high uncertainty/lose vs low uncertainty/win), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I7 (human participant groups—GAD and healthy controls are acceptable), and I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not task>baseline only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy humans investigating decision-making under outcome uncertainty with a probabilistic (60%/40%) two-alternative sampling task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and contrasts of task conditions versus an active control (information-gathering > counting; decision event > counting), with coordinates and thresholding described. Thus it meets the review’s scope (risky/probabilistic decision-making) and satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI task, task>control contrasts, whole-brain group analysis, participant eligibility, and reporting of whole-brain results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only, non-empirical) are met.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty using a probabilistic deck task with clearly defined "certain" (100:0) and "uncertain" (80:20) sequences. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., certain vs. uncertain sequences, increases vs. decreases in objective certainty) in addition to task-versus-baseline maps, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with cluster correction and peak coordinates, and reports results in tables and figures. Participant groups include OCD patients and controls (acceptable per eligibility). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI experiment in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (synchrony/asynchrony judgments) (I4). The authors report condition-versus-control contrasts appropriate for perceptual DM (e.g., asynchrony and synchrony perception > auditory+visual unisensory conditions; i.e., perceptual task > control task) (I5). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses are described and reported (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests; activation maps and tables) fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participants are healthy human adults (I7). Results are reported in text/figures/tables with coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (contrasts are not task>rest only; study is fMRI not PET; whole-brain maps are provided; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study collected whole-brain, group-level task-evoked data while human participants performed a probabilistic reward-guided decision-making task with uncertain/anti-correlated reward contingencies and reversals. The task involves decision-making under probabilistic uncertainty (risk/ambiguity) and includes within-task condition contrasts (reward vs. punishment; positive vs. negative prediction error parametric modulators) and PE-related contrasts used in whole-brain analyses. Results are reported as voxelwise group-level maps with coordinates and FWE correction. Participant groups (alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It reports within-task contrasts suitable for risky decision-making (risk/reward 25/75 vs control; high-risk 25% vs low-risk 75%) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain analysis conducted and MNI coordinates reported, with ROI/SVC follow-up). Participants are human adolescents (healthy), and whole-brain results are reported in tables/coordinates. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only rest contrasts, ROI-only without whole-brain results, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because its task is social decision-making (emotion recognition of morphed faces), which falls under exclusion criterion E5 (social decision-making is a non-qualifying task per E5). Despite exclusion, the paper does meet several inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI was conducted while participants performed an ambiguous decision-making task involving uncertain/ambiguous facial expressions), I5 (it reports within-task contrasts comparing decision events: last face > previous faces), I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported, with FWE-corrected results), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded solely because it violates E5 (task domain: social decision-making), even though it otherwise provides appropriate fMRI whole-brain contrasts and analyses.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that used four perceptual decision-making tasks (face-house, happy-angry face, audio-visual synchrony/asynchrony, and random dot motion) with manipulations of difficulty/ambiguity (noise levels, coherence, asynchrony). The authors report within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., noisy > clear, low coherence > high coherence, asynchrony > synchrony) that match the perceptual-DM contrast forms in the inclusion criteria. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM8 voxelwise results with thresholding and tables of activations/coordinates reported. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not only task>rest contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original fMRI study in humans that measured brain activation while participants performed a risky decision-making task (repeated choices between a risky stock and a safe bond). It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., stock vs. bond choice in the gain domain — equivalent to risky > safe) and conducts group-level, whole-brain analyses (SPM group-level contrasts, whole-brain FWE-corrected results reported). Participants are healthy adult males. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (experimental design, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLMs), Results (whole-brain and ROI results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study reports fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning decision task (I4 met) in human participants (I7 met), but the neuroimaging analysis was constrained to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and no unmasked whole-brain task-activation map is reported, i.e. only ROI-based results are presented (meets exclusion E6). Consequently the required whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map is not available (I6 not met), and the reported contrasts (win, lose-stay, lose-shift) do not match the explicit risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms required (I5 not met). Qualifying whole-brain results are not provided in tables/figures as whole-brain maps (I8 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-alternative perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated stimulus coherence.
