It reports within-task contrasts comparing difficulty levels (hard > easy) and DR>RT, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction and reports MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Behavioral modeling and DDM-informed analyses are included. The study therefore satisfies perceptual-decision criteria, provides condition-vs-condition contrasts (hard>easy), and supplies whole-brain group-level results (maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (monetary lotteries). The authors present within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices (behavioral and BOLD contrasts) and examine modulation by regulation (Look vs Relax). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with FDR thresholding and tables/coordinates of regions (e.g., Table 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4–I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the task is social bargaining (Ultimatum Game) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social decision-making, which is listed as an example of tasks to exclude). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions, e.g., slightly selfish > fair and fair > selfish), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported), I7 (healthy adult participants; participant groups are acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; it is social/fairness-driven UG proposing). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite having whole-brain fMRI contrasts, because the decision-making domain does not match the review focus (E5).

The study reports an fMRI experiment (BART) administered during scanning (risky decision-making), satisfying I4. It includes explicit condition-vs-control contrasts (Active Pumpsparametric vs Control Pumpsparametric; Active vs Control), satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain GLM with voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction and report coordinates and group-level results, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adult males (eligible under I7). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7) and contrasts are condition-vs-control rather than task>rest (not E3). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Overall, all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply, so the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a rewarded antisaccade (inhibitory control) task but does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (human participants; age groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (contrasts are reward vs neutral/incentive cue and preparatory/saccade epochs, not one of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis for not meeting I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI study using a mixed gambles task (50/50 gains/losses) that probes risky decision-making in human participants (adolescents and adults). The study reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Accepted Trials > Rejected Trials and Rejected Trials > Accepted Trials) as well as Accepted/Rejected trials versus baseline, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables. Participants are healthy human subjects across relevant ages. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, no ROI-only, not only baseline contrasts, and includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (gambling) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decisions after Norisk vs Riskwin; Risk vs Norisk; RA > FG > RD) and analyzes decision-related and feedback-related BOLD responses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected, GRFT) with MNI coordinates and tables; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present. The participants are healthy adults and results are clearly described in methods, results and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task (I4). The paper includes condition-vs-condition contrasts and tests of decision factors (e.g., positive vs negative EV, high vs low uncertainty, high vs low urgency, and interactions)—satisfying the required decision-making contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM8 flexible factorial second-level analysis; voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction), and whole-brain results are reported (I6, I8). Participants are healthy humans (I7), which is an eligible group. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on task>rest contrasts (it reports direct condition contrasts), is not PET, includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and is an empirical fMRI activation study. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

The study reports group-level fMRI during decision-making tasks that involve risk (probabilistic reward task and risky decision task), satisfying the requirement for fMRI during risky decision-making. Neural analyses include parametric task-related contrasts (ventral striatal BOLD correlated with expected value and reward prediction error during choice and outcome periods), which constitute within-task condition contrasts relevant to risky-DM. The methods describe whole-brain acquisition and SPM8 voxelwise analysis and display whole-brain images (reported at uncorrected P<.001), indicating group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps were produced. Participant groups (depressed and controls) are acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

Excluded because the task is a value-based cost–benefit integration without explicit risk, ambiguity, or a perceptual decision-making manipulation. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (did not implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review) and I5 (the allowed contrast forms are specified for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM; the study’s contrasts are value-based comparisons and model-driven PPIs rather than the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task) during scanning and reports within-task contrasts comparing decisions after losses vs after wins (riskloss > riskwin and vice versa). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates. The task and contrasts directly probe risky decision-making and meet the meta-analysis focus. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete for screening purposes.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants (primary care physicians) performing diagnostic decision-making tasks that explicitly manipulate diagnosticity (high vs low diagnosticity → maps to certainty/uncertainty). It includes within-task condition contrasts comparing diagnostic information of differing diagnosticity and task contrasts (diagnosis vs naming; diagnosis vs prescription), matching the required contrast types (e.g., high uncertainty/low diagnosticity vs low uncertainty/high diagnosticity). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (SPM12) with peak coordinates and FWE correction reported. Participants are an acceptable human group. Results and maps are reported in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as an ambiguous (uncertainty) decision-making fMRI study.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the probabilistic “weather prediction” task (decisions under probabilistic uncertainty), with task-versus-control contrasts (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control) and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (tables and figures). The task constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous DM), the admitted contrast form (task > control) matches I5, whole-brain voxelwise maps and second-level analyses are present (I6), participant groups (patients and healthy adults) are acceptable (I7), and results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting baseline contrasts only; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of feedback-related activation and cycle-phase interactions, but it does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) specified by the meta-analysis. Instead, reported contrasts are feedback-based (positive vs negative) and cycle-phase interactions. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrast) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-related task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy humans), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly triggered; exclusion is based on failure to meet all inclusion criteria (I5). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a decision-making task (four-armed bandit) with probabilistic rewards (risk), and thus addresses risky decision-making. It includes task-based, within-task contrasts via model-based parametric regressors (baseline prediction error and novelty-bonus-related prediction error) and contrasts comparing choices of novel versus familiar options, which qualify as decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM5 random-effects analyses (with results reported and small-volume correction for a priori regions), and participants were healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (the HiLo game). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., 50% uncertainty vs 100% certainty; linear contrasts across uncertainty levels) that directly test ambiguity-related decision processes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using FLAME with cluster correction (z>2.3, p<.05), and coordinates for significant clusters (ACC: x=-2,y=22,z=38) are reported. Participants are healthy adolescents and adults within the eligible age range. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI ambiguous decision-making, condition contrasts, and whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=20) who performed a sequential monetary gambling task involving explicit risky choices (accept vs reject). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM/SnPM) with corrected cluster results and coordinates, and condition contrasts such as accept > reject and parametric modulators (trial outcome, accumulated reward, decision value) that directly compare decision-making conditions (risky vs safe and other within-task contrasts). Full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the text, and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a sequential risk-taking task (participants open boxes with uncertain ‘devil’ outcomes), meeting risky decision-making criteria. It reports within-task contrasts (Context: Self vs Computer; Outcome: Optimum, Non-optimum, Devil) and parametric contrasts (gains, losses) rather than task>rest, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition comparisons. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM8 results with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds reported (tables/figures described). Participants are healthy human adults. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults performing risky decision-making tasks (lotteries) and social strategic games involving uncertainty. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., risky/B-choice vs sure/A-choice; entry games > lotteries/stag-hunt; non-threshold vs threshold) and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are reported; contrasts are condition-versus-condition, not task>rest; modality is fMRI). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (choices between risky and safe options). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe and high-risk versus low-risk conditions, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain activation reporting, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not resting/seed-only, not ROI-only, and includes within-group task contrasts).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated sensory evidence (high vs low coherence). The authors report within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual DM (High>Low and Low>High sensory evidence; sensory task vs baseline) and additional contrasts for motor preparation (eye/hand). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (mixed-effects FLAME1+2) voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction; results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic/uncertainty feedback task that involves anticipation of gains/losses), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the study does not report any qualifying decision-making contrast of the forms required (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, hard > easy). The main reported contrasts are valence-based (gain vs loss anticipation; gain vs loss outcomes) rather than risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty contrasts (no bivalent > non-bivalent or analogous ambiguity contrasts are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (required contrast specification) despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Exclusion: E5 met — the task is an erotic Go/NoGo response-inhibition task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (participant group is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm), I5 (contrasts are NoGo vs Go and Male vs Female motivational contrasts, which do not match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review’s decision-making domains.)

This is an fMRI study that explicitly examined risky decision-making using a Roulette task manipulating reward probability (25% vs 75%), i.e. risky versus safe conditions. It reports within-task condition contrasts (high- vs low-probability gains and related probability-by-group contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain results and supplementary tables of activated foci are described). Participant groups are human (bipolar patients and healthy controls). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not resting-state/ROI-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI and should be included.

Exclusion: E6 and E7 apply. The study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (moving dots) and compared coherence levels (12% vs 50%), so I4 and I5 are met; participant criteria I7 is met. However, the paper reports ROI-based directed connectivity (spectral Granger causality among predefined ROIs) and net causal outflows, without presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map or whole-brain contrast maps (no voxelwise 'low coherence > high coherence' activation map or coordinates/tables indicating whole-brain task activations). Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results) and E7 (only effective/connectivity analyses without whole-brain task activation map). Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (and thus I8 not applicable). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a decision-making task that manipulates risk, estimation uncertainty, and unexpected uncertainty (restless multi-armed bandit). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (FWE-corrected) and provide coordinates and figures for parametric contrasts (e.g., phasic activation correlating with risk at cue: regions showing linear increases with risk), which constitute within-task condition contrasts equivalent to high-risk > low-risk or risker > surer. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is cited but not required. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not task>rest-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (card-guessing/betting) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., self-selected vs. computer-selected trials; previous win vs. loss; interactions) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates/tables. The task and contrasts map onto risky decision-making contrasts and satisfy the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is a human fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (images of pianos/chairs) that manipulated stimulus discriminability (high/medium/low) and analysed task difficulty (decreasing stimulus quality = hard > easy) and trial-by-trial RT effects. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLMs were reported with FWE-corrected results and clusters in tables/figures. Contrasts correspond to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low > high stimulus quality / hard > easy), satisfying the review’s contrast requirements. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Although the study employed fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and reports a risky > safe contrast, all reported fMRI analyses were conducted using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume corrections. The paper does not present unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making) and I5 (risky > safe contrast) and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps). Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study that implements a probabilistic (ambiguous) decision-making task (modified beads task) performed during BOLD fMRI in human participants (schizophrenia patients and controls). The paper reports within-task contrasts (lake reasoning > color naming; last fish with decision > preceding fish) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects, FWE-corrected results) with coordinates and tables/figures. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for an ambiguous decision-making task, an active task-versus-control contrast, whole-brain group-level activation maps, and participant groups within the eligible set. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

This fMRI study examined perceptual decision-making (face gender discrimination) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (reward bias vs neutral; evidence vs noise), and used healthy human participants — thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts such as evidence vs noise and reward bias vs neutral), and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). However, the reported analyses and results are exclusively ROI-based time-course analyses (effector- and stimulus-selective ROIs) with no clear report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps, coordinates, or whole-brain tables/figures in the provided full text. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Exclusion criteria met: E6. Full text appears complete for screening (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Given the absence of unmasked whole-brain task activation results, this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that directly manipulates outcome probability (risk) within a decision-making task (options with differing probabilities and delays) and reports group-level whole-brain task-versus-control contrasts. The authors present a decision-making condition contrasted against active control tasks (summation and visual controls) and report voxelwise random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Although the paradigm also includes delay, the critical manipulation involves probabilistic (risky) choices and a parametric subjective-value regressor; thus it fits the meta-analysis scope of risky decision-making. Full text (methods, results, figures, tables, and coordinates) is available. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI was conducted while participants performed a risky gamble task interleaved with the social PD), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (healthy participants were tested), I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 — the paper does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast of the form required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, or an explicit risky decision > control-task contrast). The gamble task analyses model outcome (e.g., $0, $1, $2) and use outcome-based contrasts and a task-by-payoff interaction ((CD-CC)-($0-$2)), rather than a direct risky-versus-safe or decision-phase contrast. Therefore it does not provide the required decision-making condition contrast for inclusion. Full text appears complete, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) during scanning, with within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (pump decisions following negative feedback/explosion vs following positive feedback/cash-out). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates, cluster-corrected maps, NeuroVault link). Participant sample and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the Decision-Reward Uncertainty Task examining risky and uncertain decision-making and reward outcomes. It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (behavioral risk > reward risk/no-risk; reward > no-reward) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures. The full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky/uncertainty decision-making (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), connectivity/resting-only criteria do not apply, and within-group/main-effect maps are reported (not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Given these points, I include this study in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports a behavioral study of probabilistic reinforcement learning in adults with ASD and typically developing controls; no fMRI scanning or neuroimaging data were collected or reported. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant groups qualify). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no reported within-task or task>control contrasts from imaging data), I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but it lacks any imaging/whole-brain activation results required for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet the core imaging-related inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing the risky-gains task (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts (risky > safe) at the subject level and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 t-maps with voxel-wise threshold and cluster extent), and present activation tables/figures. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (risky > safe) with whole-brain group maps; no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, baseline-only contrasts, ROI-only reporting) are met.

This is an fMRI study using an instrumental probabilistic (80% vs 20%) reinforcement-learning task (choices between stimuli with probabilistic reward/punishment), satisfying the review’s focus on decision-making under uncertainty (risky DM). The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (rewarded > non-rewarded; punished > non-punished; reward > punishment) and parametric prediction-error regressors, with standard random-effects whole-brain analyses and ROI/whole-brain results reported. Participants include clinical and healthy groups. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a Wheel of Fortune task manipulating reward magnitude, probability, and risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts including risky > safe (risk contrast), probability contrasts (low vs high), and magnitude contrasts (high vs low) during the selection phase. Group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses are reported with coordinate tables and corrected cluster thresholds. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a perceptual decision-making task (GO/NO-GO). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM) for parametric contrasts and categorical contrasts across levels of predictive information (within-task condition comparisons), including conjunctions and clusterwise/FWE-corrected inference. Results are reported in the text and supplemental tables/figures. Thus the paper provides whole-brain, task-evoked activation maps for perceptual decision-making contrasts (decision-related parametric and categorical contrasts), meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (sparse vs dense categorization with an uncertainty opt-out), includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., uncertainty > correct categorization, correct > uncertainty, and parametric distance-to-bound modulators corresponding to difficulty/hard>easy), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies fMRI during perceptual decision-making (I4), includes relevant condition-vs-condition contrasts (I5), provides whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I6), has an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study used event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy humans and reports coordinate-based results (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm examining reversal learning and responses to negative feedback, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses, probabilistic errors vs correct, etc.) do not match the required decision-making contrasts (I5 not met). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty/ambiguity in reward outcomes (risky/ambiguous decision-making). The authors report voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level analyses of task-related parametric modulators (expected value/high vs low and positive prediction error), with thresholding and cluster correction and within-group maps and between-group comparisons (controls vs depressed vs suicide attempters). Participant groups are acceptable. Results are presented as whole-brain maps, figures, and tables. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans that administered a mixed gain–loss gambling task (risky decision-making) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts of decision-related activity. The paper presents within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of decision phase by gain–loss ratio; linear and quadratic effects; within-group and between-group contrasts) rather than only task>baseline, and reports whole-brain SPM8 results with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level inference. Participants include both pathological gamblers and healthy controls (acceptable per eligibility). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state/connectivity-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides usable whole-brain activation results.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic feedback decision task (choices between high/low with 83%/67%/50% reward probabilities) performed during scanning. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (with cluster correction) and provide coordinates/tables for activations. They model and test trial-by-trial uncertainty (a parametric modulator) and other decision-related contrasts (action values, action-dependent and action-independent prediction errors), which correspond to contrasts of high vs low uncertainty / action-dependent decision signals. Participants were healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a decision task with uncertainty), I5 (decision-related contrasts via parametric modulators, e.g., uncertainty/high vs low), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports empirical fMRI data collected while human participants made risky and ambiguous decision-making choices (I4). It includes condition-wise comparisons and parametric contrasts (subjective value under ambiguity vs risk; ambiguous > risk) and thus meets the contrast requirement (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with corrected thresholds and reported activation maps/tables (I6, I8). Participants are healthy human volunteers (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only task>baseline contrasts, and is empirical. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and figures/tables descriptions, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports event-related fMRI data collected while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), satisfying I4. The authors created condition-versus-condition contrasts (win minus neutral; loss minus neutral) and modeled response and feedback phases, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (independent t-tests; results reported with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values, with small-volume correction noted), satisfying I6. Participant groups (ADHD and healthy controls) are acceptable per I7. Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in the text/figures, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET modality, only ROI results, task>rest only contrasts, or only connectivity/resting-state analyses) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

Exclusion (E5): The study uses a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/episodic memory task and investigates prediction-error-related activity and memory, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported/mentioned), I7 (human participant groups qualifying by age/health), I8 (whole-brain results referenced in main/supplemental materials). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM tasks required), I5 (no accepted decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Because I4 and I5 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded under E5.

Excluded under E5: the task is a probabilistic category-learning (weather prediction) nondeclarative learning task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The study does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (it reports a task > active control contrast: weather prediction > perceptual-motor control), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM99), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). However I4 is not met because the experimental task is a category-learning/memory task, not a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty decision-making task per the meta-analysis definitions. Full text appears complete and was reviewed in detail.

The study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain, group-level analyses (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (I8). However, the task is a noninstrumental, deterministic outcome-prediction task using appetitive and aversive cues without any manipulation of risk, uncertainty/ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty; it therefore does not satisfy I4 (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) nor I5 (relevant decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). This violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (the cups task) (I4), and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., risky > safe; win > loss; parametric risk/reward contrasts) (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise maps with reported MNI coordinates and GRF-corrected thresholds (I6) and results are reported for eligible participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) (I7). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that manipulated reward probability (risk) within an economic decision task and analyzed task-evoked BOLD responses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM) with task-versus-control contrasts (DM > C2) and regression analyses using entropy; results are reported as clusters/coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (decision task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning task with monetary rewards and punishments, which constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (risky/ambiguous DM). The experiment collected whole-brain task-evoked fMRI data during the task and reports whole-brain one-sample and between-group voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected), including contrasts separating punished and rewarded trials and correlations with computational model parameters. These meet the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during a risky/ambiguous decision-making task, (I5) within-task condition contrasts (punished vs rewarded and parametric modulators), (I6) whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported, (I7) allowed participant groups (adolescent patients and healthy controls), and (I8) clear reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study that includes a probability discounting task (risky decision-making) performed during scanning and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The authors computed contrasts/parametric regressors for subjective value separately for probability (PD) and delay (DD) trials, conducted comparisons between PD and DD (regions showing better correlations for PD than DD and vice versa), and conjunction analyses. Results are reported as whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and figures (supplemental tables). The sample is healthy human participants. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This study meets the review criteria. It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying I4. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (parametric PE regressors and group contrasts), satisfying I6 and I8. The paper includes between-condition contrasts comparing decision-making contexts (reward-seeking vs punishment-avoidance) and stimulus-domain conditions (faces vs abstract), which are valid within-task decision-making condition contrasts for the meta-analysis (satisfying I5). Participants are a healthy human sample (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only task>baseline implicit contrasts (they include between-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-choice monetary risk-taking), explicitly tested contrasts comparing decision conditions (risky > safe and related contrasts), and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster-corrected results, tables, and figures). Participant groups (alcohol-dependent patients and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition, whole-brain analysis), Results (within- and between-group contrasts, cumulative-earnings modulation), and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human volunteers performing a risky decision-making task (risky £1 vs safer 10p choices) inside the scanner. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses identifying neural correlates of decision-related parametric modulators (choice temperature βm and learning rate αm) and contrasts comparing ketamine vs placebo sessions (paired t-tests). These constitute within-task, condition-related task contrasts (trial-wise high vs low decision-related signals) and not task>rest contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps (cluster-corrected) and described in the text. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only, and includes within-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (lotteries) inside the scanner. The authors performed group-level GLM analyses including parametric modulators (ΔU, ΔMin, ΔEV), compared task conditions (Self vs Other; Comp filler), and report whole-brain activation results (with summary tables) and ROI analyses. Thus it provides within-task contrasts/parametric task effects relevant to risk decision-making, and includes group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results. Participants are healthy university students. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI or connectivity results, contrasts only vs baseline) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

The study reports an fMRI task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) administered during scanning to human participants (I4). It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions: choose win > choose inflate (choice-phase) and outcome inflate > explode (outcome-phase), which map onto risky decision-making contrasts (I5). The authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise permutation testing (group-level task-evoked whole-brain analysis is described), even though no clusters survived correction; this satisfies I6 (whole-brain analysis was performed and reported). The sample (youth with ADHD/DBD) is an eligible participant group (I7). Whole-brain analyses and their (null) results are described in the text, satisfying I8. Although significant effects were reported only in ROI analyses, the presence and reporting of the group-level whole-brain analysis means the study meets inclusion rather than being excluded under E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing decision-making tasks involving risk/ambiguity (IGT and RDT). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (parametric contrasts for reward and risk prediction errors), conjunction and contrast analyses including IGT > RDT, and whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected maps with coordinates. Results are reported in tables/figures and supplemental material. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision tasks), I5 (between-task contrast IGT > RDT and task-related parametric contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy participants allowed), and I8 (coordinates and maps reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task). The authors report a within-task contrast 'risky decisions minus safe decisions' (risky > safe), performed at the group-level using random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (statistical parametric maps, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds) and report coordinates/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets fMRI task (I4), appropriate decision-making contrast (I5), whole-brain group-level analysis (I6), participant eligibility (I7), and reporting of coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing the Paper-Scissors-Rock (PSR) decision-making task, which uses predetermined probabilities for preferred/even/worst responses (90%, 50%, 10%), constituting risky/uncertain decision-making. The analyses include within-task contrasts among decision conditions (preferred, even, worst) rather than only task>baseline contrasts, satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making condition contrast. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps were generated and reported (LME voxelwise tests, cluster correction, tables/figures of significant clusters), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participant groups (occasional stimulant users) are acceptable per eligibility. Results are reported in the main text and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to task>rest only, not PET, not ROI-only, and include whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a multi-attribute decision-making task where trials systematically varied the variability (ambiguity) of value predictions. The authors explicitly decoded variability (sorted into four groups) and tested where in the brain variability/ambiguity information was represented, performing group-level, voxelwise second-level statistics on whole-brain searchlight accuracy maps and reporting MNI coordinates. This constitutes a condition-vs-condition (high vs low variability/ambiguity) analysis appropriate for ambiguous decision-making contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports whole-brain coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human healthy adults using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky > safe; punishment feedback > risky; multiple punished-then-risky and risky-then-risky contrasts) and subject- and group-level analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001 with cluster correction; tables/figures and ROI results are provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not PET, not task>rest only, includes whole-brain results beyond ROI).

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary decision-making task varying reward probability and magnitude (uncertainty/risk), satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., 50% vs 100%), reward magnitude and value, and prediction error contrasts, satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level analyses with FDR/FWE correction and coordinate tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults, satisfying I7. The manuscript includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts indexing risk (parametric modulation by pump number; effectively high-risk > low-risk) and include control pump events (white balloons) to account for motor/visual activity. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME1; voxelwise Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (a risky/probabilistic decision-making paradigm). It reports within-task contrasts decoding behavioral decisions (switch vs. stay) based on trial-wise neural activity, which constitutes a within-task decision-making contrast relevant to risky/uncertain decisions. The paper includes group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain visualizations (Fig. 2B) and describes voxelwise analyses and preprocessing, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants were healthy humans, and whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrast — switch vs. stay), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans using a risky decision-making task (accept/reject mixed gambles with 50% win/loss probability). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts (e.g., anticipation/activation for losses vs gains, bidirectional responses, acceptance > rejection) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM8; thresholds reported). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This fMRI study used the BIAS financial decision-making task (stocks vs bond) manipulating uncertainty/risk and measured BOLD while participants made choices. It reports task contrasts relevant to the review (neural representation of uncertainty as a parametric modulation, and comparisons preceding bond vs stock choices — i.e., risk-avoidant vs risk-seeking), at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported clusters, tables/figures). Participants include clinical (violent offenders subgroups) and healthy controls, which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (with tables/figures referenced). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study using a gambling (risky decision-making) task with within-task contrasts (risky vs non-risky and parametric effects related to risk) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making (I4, I5), provides whole-brain voxelwise group results (I6), and participant sampling is acceptable (I7); results are reported with coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps while participants performed a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with volatile (high uncertainty) and stable (low uncertainty) decision-making conditions. The authors report within-task contrasts (learning-rate-modulation/volatile trials vs nonlearning/stable trials) and model-based regressors (RPE and learning rate) with whole-brain analyses and tables, satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements analogous to 'high uncertainty > low uncertainty'. The task engages decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous/risky DM), and participants include healthy and schizophrenia groups (eligible populations). Whole-brain results are reported (tables/figures) and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in human participants performing a decision-making task that explicitly manipulates risk and ambiguity. Behavioral and fMRI analyses include condition-versus-condition contrasts (ambiguity > risk and main effect of condition), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported cluster coordinates/tables. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable per the review. Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures; contrasts are not against implicit baseline only. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>rest-only) are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (olfactory 2AFC), directly addressing perceptual DM. The authors conducted within-task comparisons and model-based regressions that distinguish difficulty/temporal-integration profiles (analogous to hard > easy or condition-wise contrasts) and tested condition-by-time interactions. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain GLMs (subject-level contrasts entered into a one-sample t test) with reported significant activations and follow-up ROI deconvolution. Participants are healthy adults and full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Gabor orientation discrimination) with on-trial subjective certainty ratings. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (correct-unsure vs correct-sure; correct > error), which correspond to high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty / perceptual difficulty contrasts. Whole-brain group analyses (FLAME1) and cluster-corrected maps are reported in text, tables, and figures. Participants are within the eligible population. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task vs rest-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used an experiential risky decision-making task (choices between sure and risky monetary options). The paper reports within-task contrasts and model-based regressors (e.g., RSTD prediction error; contrasts comparing risk-related trials to other trials) and performs a group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analysis with familywise error correction, reporting surviving clusters and coordinates (Table 1). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts/model regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task) and tests contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., decision after loss vs decision after win; feedback risk win vs risk loss). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded with cluster correction; peak coordinates and cluster tables are reported. Participants include healthy controls and frequent poker players. The task is a risky DM paradigm and the reported contrasts are within-task condition comparisons, thus meeting the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making contrasts. Full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and imaging), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study reports empirical fMRI data from 143 healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (gain/loss framing). It includes within-task condition contrasts (frame-consistent vs frame-inconsistent choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (unthresholded framing contrast deposited on NeuroVault). Methods, results, and discussion are present and detailed. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during risky decision-making, (I5) at least one condition-vs-condition contrast, (I6) whole-brain group-level maps, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) clearly described whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not against implicit baseline, not PET, not ROI-only, etc.). Full text appears complete.

This study acquired fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), and reports within-task contrasts (loseshift > winstay; final error > error) that compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with multiple-comparison correction and reported coordinates/figures/tables. Participant groups (schizophrenia and controls) are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). Contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), it is not PET, and it provides whole-brain results rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a four-armed bandit gambling task involving decision-making under uncertainty (exploration vs exploitation), which qualifies as risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports a within-task contrast classifying trials as exploratory versus exploitative (a decision-vs-decision comparison). Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and report whole-brain-corrected activations and peak coordinates (figures and coordinates are provided). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore the study satisfies I4 (fMRI + human decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task decision contrasts: exploratory > exploitative), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with corrections), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, discussion, and coordinates (supplementary methods referenced but core content present).

This study reports an fMRI experiment using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task, with participants scanned while performing active-choice and passive-no-choice conditions. It presents within-task risk-level contrasts (parametric modulation of probability of explosion; effectively high-risk > low-risk comparisons) and an active-choice vs passive-no-choice contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise, with multiple-comparison cluster correction; results are reported as clusters/coordinates and figures. Participants are human young adults (twins), and whole-brain task activation maps are described and used for voxelwise genetic modeling. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure amounts and gambles with varying probabilities/magnitudes). It includes within-task contrasts addressing risk levels (high-risk vs low-risk loss conditions) and feedback effects, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with familywise-error correction (i.e., whole-brain statistical maps). Participant groups (binge drinkers and healthy volunteers) are acceptable. Whole-brain results are described in text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; contains within-task condition contrasts rather than only task>baseline; reports whole-brain activation maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is INCLUDED.

This study reports fMRI data collected while participants performed a probability discounting task (probability option vs fixed/certain option), which is a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper includes within-task contrasts (probability > fixed) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level analyses with cluster correction) and reports brain regions/coordinates. Although the study also includes delay-discounting (intertemporal) tasks (which would be excluded), the presence of the probability discounting task satisfies the review’s requirement for a risky decision-making fMRI contrast. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, or reporting only between-group contrasts) are met. Full text contains Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task. The fMRI analysis includes parametric modulation by pump number (capturing high-risk vs low-risk within trials) and contrasts including active (reward) vs control (white balloon) trials. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and coordinates), with mixed-effects between-subject analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition, task, GLM), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study of risky decision-making (sequential gambling ‘pig’ task) in healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators (e.g., “continue” trials modulated by cumulative gambling, stop probability) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical maps (one-sample t tests, whole-brain thresholds, and cluster-level FWE), with coordinates and SVC results. Participants are healthy volunteers. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables described, discussion).

Although this is a whole-brain fMRI study of human participants performing a probabilistic choice task (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the reported contrasts focus on outcome processing (gain vs neutral, loss vs neutral), prediction-error regressors, and functional connectivity. The paper does not report any decision-phase contrasts that match the meta-analysis requirements (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy) nor a decision-task versus active control contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI investigation of decision-making under uncertainty using a modified “beads” task (ambiguous decision-making). It includes an explicit task-versus-active-control contrast (DECISION > COUNTING), performed as whole-brain, group-level analyses (SPM5) with coordinates and figures reported. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no implicit-baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic instrumental learning task with binary choices between cues associated with different reward probabilities (25% vs 75%), which constitutes risky decision-making. The authors provide group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical parametric maps for task-related effects: parametric modulators of state value and of left/right option values at cue onset, and prediction errors at outcome. These parametric contrasts constitute within-task decision-related contrasts (i.e., neural correlates of value/risk across conditions) suitable for inclusion. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

Although the study acquired whole‑brain group fMRI data during a task involving risk (detection probability) and reports Dis vs Hon contrasts at the outcome phase, it is a social/moral dishonesty paradigm rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision‑making task. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is social/moral decision‑making (dishonesty) which the metaanalysis excludes. Moreover, the reported fMRI contrasts focus on outcome presentation (Dis vs Hon at feedback) rather than decision‑period contrasts of interest (e.g., risky > safe); therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one decision‑making contrast) is not met in this paper. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky/uncertain task), I6 (group-level whole‑brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole‑brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no decision‑period risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Given E5 is met, the study must be excluded from the decision‑making meta‑analysis.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (disadvantageous decks vs advantageous decks — corresponding to risky > safe) as well as decision > baseline contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group and between-group statistical maps (whole-brain corrected thresholds reported). Participant samples are acceptable per inclusion criteria. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making with whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, includes whole-brain maps beyond ROI or connectivity-only results, and reports within-group task effects).

This study used fMRI to measure BOLD responses to passive viewing of random-dot motion while participants performed an orthogonal fixation task; it did not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task about the motion stimuli, nor did it report decision-making contrasts. Analyses focus on retinotopically-defined ROI averages rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore it fails the key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choice between high-risk and low-risk options). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests) with thresholding and lists activation foci (Table 1, figures) for contrasts/ regressors related to decision variables (difference in weights/high-risk vs low-risk representation and reward prediction errors). The task and analyses therefore satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for (1) fMRI during risky decision-making, (2) condition-wise/task-vs-control-type contrasts via model-derived decision regressors (high- vs low-risk value difference and prediction error), (3) group-level whole-brain statistical maps, (4) an acceptable participant sample (healthy adults), and (5) reporting of whole-brain results in figures/tables. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study used fMRI while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (ring-size discrimination), and it contrasted stimulus/choice conditions, so it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM) and I5 (within-task stimulus/choice contrasts). Participants were healthy adults (I7). However, the analyses are restricted to V1 (retinotopically defined ROI/population analyses) and the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; results are presented as ROI-based/region-specific analyses rather than whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it fails I6 and matches exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). On that basis the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that directly contrasts decision-making under ambiguity and risk, reporting condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > risky, risk effects) during the decision phase. The analysis used group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistics with cluster and voxel thresholds reported, and results are described in the text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging and behavioral), results, and discussion, so the full article appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task probing reward sensitivity and cognitive flexibility, not explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts required by the review. The reported contrasts (reward vs punishment; shift vs stay) do not match accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore Exclusion E5 applies. The study does satisfy whole-brain group-level fMRI reporting and acceptable reporting formats (I6, I8) and uses human participant groups that are admissible (I7). Inclusion criteria I4 (task is a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (at least one accepted risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E5 applies. This study’s reported fMRI contrast is Win > No Win (reward receipt vs no reward) from the feedback phase, which is reward receipt without an uncertainty manipulation and not a decision-phase contrast comparing risk levels. Inclusion: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) is satisfied because the Wheel of Fortune is a risky-DM paradigm; I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps) is satisfied — whole-brain ANCOVA results are reported; I7 (participant group acceptable) is satisfied; I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) is satisfied. Inclusion not met: I5 is not met — the paper does not report a decision-making contrast of interest for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or risk > certainty); the only analyzed/ reported contrast isolates reward receipt (Win > No Win) across all trial types. Therefore the study should be excluded from the decision-making meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains). It reports within-group and between-group, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses including a risky > safe contrast (risky vs safe choices) and reward vs punishment contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain analyses with tables/figures and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (risky fMRI task; appropriate contrasts; whole-brain group-level maps; acceptable participant group; coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.
