This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic classification task that manipulates uncertainty (entropy) — an ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper includes condition-vs-condition and parametric contrasts relevant to decision-making (e.g., negative feedback vs positive feedback, and BOLD correlated with increasing entropy/high vs low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM99 second-level analyses, with FDR and cluster corrections), and coordinates/tables are provided. Although the entropy effect was significant within a predefined midbrain ROI rather than surviving whole-brain correction, the study did perform whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain results for other contrasts, and therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete in the provided content.

This fMRI study does not investigate one of the target decision-making domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) in the way required by the review. Although it uses fMRI in humans (and reports whole-brain searchlight RSA) and involves choices about probabilistic inferences, the task is an inference-about-latent-causes paradigm and the neuroimaging analyses are representational-similarity/model-fitting (RSA) rather than standard condition-vs-condition task contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria requiring a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task contrast (I4, I5) and the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrast map as the target (I6). Included: I7 (participant group acceptable). Excluded criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (18–25 y) who performed an in-scanner reward/anticipation task with uncertainty and subsequent out-of-scanner risky choice, i.e. a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., possible win anticipation vs neutral; a parametric uncertain reward-expectancy regressor) that compare decision-making conditions rather than implicit baseline. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain multiple regression in SPM with FWE correction and reported peaks). Participant groups are acceptable per criteria and whole-brain results are described. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to implicit baseline contrasts, not PET, the task is risky decision-making (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the study is empirical fMRI task activation work. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study used fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task (I4), reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), included healthy participants (I7), and presented whole-brain results in text/figures (I8), it does not report a decision-making contrast that matches the meta-analysis inclusion forms (e.g., risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The primary reported contrasts are reward vs neutral, loss vs neutral, and parametric prediction-error regressors rather than the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are triggered. Therefore excluded for failing to meet I5.

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (risk-taking and gamble stages). The authors present condition-versus-condition contrasts (risk-disadvantageous vs risk-advantageous) and group comparisons (IGD vs HC) based on second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables/figures. Participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full article contains methods, results, and discussion (full text complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only task>rest contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that manipulated probabilistic (risky) decision-making (Gambling blocks) and deterministic rule-based choices, and reports contrasts between decision conditions (e.g., low vs. high choice certainty; complex rule-based vs. high-certainty probabilistic). Group-level voxelwise analyses and activation foci are reported (tables and SPM analyses), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task and contrasts directly address risky/probabilistic decision-making relevant to the review. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (risky) monetary decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric correlations (EV vs RM, TD error, uncertainty) and conjunction analyses—i.e., condition-versus-condition effects rather than task>rest. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain/random-effects SPM results with voxelwise statistics and reported peak coordinates (with whole-brain and SVC corrections). Participants are healthy adults. Results and coordinates are fully reported in the main text and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulates outcome uncertainty in a decision task (2-choice certain vs 4-choice uncertain reversal learning). It includes a within-subject contrast that directly tests uncertainty effects (4-choice > 2-choice) on responses to unexpected non-reinforcement relative to expected reinforcement, which maps onto ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise (FSL/FEAT; Z-thresholding and cluster correction), and results are reported as coordinate tables and figures. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not baseline-only contrasts; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical; includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E6 (reporting focuses on ROI analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy human participants). Inclusion NOT met: I4 (fMRI was acquired during a Monetary Incentive Delay task, which probes reward anticipation/receipt rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; primary contrasts were win vs no-win outcomes), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported; analyses focused on basal ganglia ROIs). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy human participants performing a gambling/guessing task with uncertainty. It includes task contrasts comparing predicting (guessing) versus reporting (an active control) and difficulty contrasts (suit > colour, hard > easy), analyzed with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM methods and reported as activation foci/figures. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (decision task > control and hard>easy contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (human participants; healthy sample), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, etc.). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney face detection) and a dual-task design that separates decision from motor response. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (voxelwise maps, RFX contrasts and tables of coordinates) and data-driven ICA corroboration. Relevant within-task contrasts compare decision-related regressors (Decision_response, Decision_color) against stimulus and motor regressors, providing condition-versus-condition contrasts that index perceptual decision processes. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, task, image acquisition, GLM/ICA analysis), Results (behavioral, GLM, ICA, event-related averages) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This empirical paper reports multiple fMRI experiments in which human participants made risky/ambiguous decisions (probability-weighting and regret experiments using probabilistic electric-shock lotteries and choice among lotteries/doors). The manuscript reports within-subject condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., different probabilities; high-regret > no-regret; rejoice vs regret interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and tables of regions. Participants are healthy adults. Although the chapter also summarizes an intertemporal (dread) experiment (intertemporal choice is excluded if sole focus), the presence of the probability-weighting and regret experiments provides direct risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts suitable for the meta-analysis. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for methods and results reporting relevant contrasts.

This article reports an fMRI study in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (the BART) during scanning, includes within-task contrasts (parametric risk modulation; experimental green (risk) > control orange balloon; decision contrasts cash > inflate), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and coordinate tables. The sample and methods are fully described in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential ‘boxes’ gamble). Analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators (e.g., magnitude of missed opportunity; loss position) and second-level random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain SPM8 analyses with multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Contrasts are condition-versus-condition/parametric (not only task>baseline). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study with human participants performing a monetary risky decision-making task (gamble choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The authors used within-task parametric contrasts comparing neural responses across probability levels (linear p term and nonlinear deviation Δ(p)), and report whole-brain random-effects results (tables and figures) identifying regions (e.g., striatum) correlated with those decision variables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (experimental paradigm, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and fMRI results with tables/figures), and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) with within-subject condition contrasts. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Play > Pass, Gain > Loss, and their interaction), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster- and FWE-correction, and provides coordinates in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses an abstract moral/social value word forced-choice task (individualistic vs collectivistic) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is moral/social decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual) and E3 (the main modeled decision contrast collapses all trials into one decision condition assessed against an implicit baseline; no qualifying condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results and peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (no qualifying decision-condition versus decision-condition or experimental task versus active control contrast). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study reports fMRI during a risk-sensitivity decision-making task (choices between larger risky vs smaller certain rewards), and presents within-task contrasts (categorical regressors for selecting the variable/risky option versus not, and parametric subjective value regressors). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and ROI analyses are also described. Participants are healthy young adults and results are fully described across methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision contrasts such as variable/risky option selected vs not, and value-related regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to task>baseline contrasts only; includes condition contrasts and parametric effects; not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making (animal detection) task with manipulated motivation. Relevant contrasts meeting the review definitions are reported (NEGATIVE > NEUTRAL, POSITIVE > NEUTRAL; task blocks also contrasted against an active arrow baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (FWE-corrected whole-brain tables and figures), and ROI results are supplementary — i.e., whole-brain results are available. The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm (detection), so it fits the perceptual-DM category. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not PET, not rest-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study administering a probabilistic (beads) decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (ambiguous decision-making). It includes within-task contrasts suitable for the meta-analysis (lake decision > colour decision; last fish > all previous fish), including an explicit task-versus-control contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8; FWE-corrected whole-brain results and coordinate tables) alongside ROI checks. Participant groups (ARMS patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. Results and coordinates are fully described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not only baseline contrasts; whole-brain maps reported; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study with human participants performing a decision task that explicitly manipulates ambiguity (ambiguous context vs. generalization context) and examines neural correlates of ambiguity during choices. The task contrasts high-ambiguity and low-ambiguity conditions and uses a model-based (Shannon entropy) regressor indexing ambiguity, which was tested at the group level. Analyses include whole-brain SPM second-level results with cluster-level FWE correction and ROI analyses; whole-brain activations for ambiguity (right hippocampus/amygdala, fusiform/precuneus) are reported. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI human ambiguous decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts: high vs low ambiguity / ambiguity parametric regressor), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (healthy participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used the Cups task (risky decision-making) during fMRI (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., ADV Risk > DIS Risk and other EV contrasts) that directly compare decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise FLAME results with cluster correction and reported activation tables/figures (meets I6 and I8). Participant groups (healthy adolescents and adults) are acceptable (meets I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (detecting degraded fearful vs neutral faces) while BOLD data were acquired. The paper presents condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., fear-cue vs neutral-cue; fearful-face vs neutral-face; FC/FF vs NC/FF) rather than task>baseline contrasts, and conducts group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (paired t-tests and mixed-model ANOVA) with reported whole-brain results and ROI-corrected results. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps from a perceptual decision-making paradigm. All relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (ambiguous) decision-making task (Box Task). It reports within-task contrasts including conclusion > draw and, critically, a high-uncertainty versus low-uncertainty contrast (60:40 > 80:20), satisfying the ambiguous decision-making comparison. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with reported activation maps/tables and PPI connectivity; whole-brain task-evoked results are presented in tables/figures/text. Full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing an ecologically valid risky decision-making task (virtual sexual ‘hook up’ game) during scanning (meets I4). It reports condition-vs-condition contrasts including SRD > Conversational (an active control) and SRD > implicit baseline (meets I5). Group-level voxelwise/statistical maps and TFCE cluster results with peak coordinates are reported for task contrasts and between-group comparisons (reported clusters/coordinates and whole-brain covariate analyses), satisfying whole-brain, group-level reporting (I6) and coordinate reporting (I8). Participant sample (MSM, including meth users and non-users) is an acceptable participant group (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not only against implicit baseline (E3 not met), not PET (E4), task is risky decision-making (E5 not met), whole-brain results/coordinates are reported (E6 not met), and this is empirical fMRI activation (E7, E8 not met). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (fMRI-adapted BART) with a clear active vs passive task contrast (active>passive). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects) with cluster-corrected results, tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (task vs active control contrast), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not a PET, not only ROI or connectivity, contrasts are task vs control not baseline, and contains within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced).

This paper reports an fMRI study in humans performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/uncertain decision-making task), and analyzes trial-to-trial prediction-error as a parametric regressor (a within-task contrast). The manuscript includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (two-sample t tests with cluster correction) and reports within-group one-sample effects of the prediction-error regressor. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: prediction-error parametric modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria appear to apply (not PET, not task>rest only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches with manipulated discriminability/contrast). The analysis included within-task comparisons that index perceptual difficulty/discriminability (high- vs low-contrast trials, implemented via trial-by-trial parametric regressors and model comparisons), and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM2 random-effects ANOVA with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates). Participants were healthy adults. The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). Although the paper used fMRI with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I6), included qualifying participant groups (ASD and controls) (I7), and reported whole-brain results in tables/figures (I8), it did not implement a decision-making task nor report contrasts that compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The fMRI contrasts are stimulation (texture) > rest (baseline) and within- and between-group texture effects, not decision-making condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts; thus I4 and I5 are not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with within-task motivational manipulation (motivated vs neutral) — addressing I4 and providing a condition-versus-condition contrast (motivated > neutral) that qualifies as a decision-making contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (second-level random-effects, whole-brain FWE-corrected results) satisfying I6. Participant groups (medicated schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable per I7. Results are described in full text (tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups), meeting I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., contrasts are not only versus implicit baseline, whole-brain maps are provided, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a naturalistic risky decision-making task). The analysis includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (prepump vs pre-cash out; i.e., risky vs safe) and univariate contrast maps, whole-brain searchlight and whole-brain classifier analyses at the group level. Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The task directly assesses risky decision-making and meets the meta-analysis definitions for risky-DM contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that explicitly examines decision making under risk (explicit probabilities and incentives), using blocked task conditions. It reports a within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast comparing the information-based risk decision condition (A) to an active high-level control condition (B) and provides group-level random-effects results with coordinates. Participants are healthy elderly adults. Whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates).

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents that implemented a risky vs ambiguous decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) during scanning, reported condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Risk Gamble > Ambiguity Gamble, Ambiguity Gamble > Risk Gamble, Gain > No Gain), and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster correction and MNI coordinates. Participants are a healthy adolescent sample (11–24 yrs). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that administered a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task during scanning and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results. The fMRI analyses include parametric contrasts directly testing decision parameters (e.g., |p-0.5| reflecting high uncertainty > low uncertainty, EV-related correlations) and report cluster-level corrected whole-brain maps. Participants are healthy human volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, enabling assessment of task contrasts and whole-brain statistics. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with within-task contrasts (rewarded vs nonrewarded; directional probability contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with statistical maps and tables of coordinates, including t-maps and corrected peaks. Participants are healthy humans and full article includes methods, results, and discussion. These elements satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and do not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating outcome uncertainty. The task contrasts two-choice prediction (decision under uncertainty) with an active control (two-choice response task) and explicitly tests an uncertainty contrast (50% error rate vs 20%/80% error rates; contrast vector = high uncertainty > low uncertainty). The analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster correction) with group-level mixed-model ANOVA and coordinates/figures reported. Participants include schizophrenia subjects and matched healthy controls. Reporting includes task-versus-control and uncertainty-related contrasts, and whole-brain maps/tables/figures. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (feedback processing and behavioral adaptation) rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The reported contrasts compare error versus correct responses or switch versus nonswitch errors, not the canonical contrasts required for risky (e.g., risky>safe), ambiguous (e.g., high uncertainty>low uncertainty), or perceptual (e.g., hard>easy) decision-making. Although the study provides group-level whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates and includes healthy human participants, it does not meet the required task/contrast definitions for inclusion. Therefore it is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (coordinates and whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM by the review definitions), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (50:50 monetary gambles), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinate tables; participants are an acceptable sample and results are reported with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise analysis), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (coordinates/figures reported). However, the imaging results do not report a contrast that directly compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, accept > reject, high-risk > low-risk) or an experimental risk task > control task. The primary reported contrast is novel > familiar prime and regressions of that contrast with subsequent risk-taking behavior; no within-task decision-making contrast (risky vs safe) is provided in the reported whole-brain results. Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 is not met.

Although this fMRI study used a probabilistic (65% vs 35%) reward-learning task (meets I4) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I6) with results described in the text/tables (meets I8) and an eligible participant sample (meets I7), it does not include any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, or an explicit decision-task > control-task contrast). The reported analyses focus on parametric RPE and value regressors and emotional (fearful vs neutral) modulations, not on between-condition decision-making contrasts of risk/ambiguity or hard>easy perceptual difficulty. Therefore Inclusion Criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are directly met, but failure to meet I5 mandates exclusion.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that directly investigates risky financial decision-making (BIAS task) during event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript reports voxelwise group maps and condition contrasts (e.g., stock gain > loss, market relative gain > loss, stock vs bond choice) with thresholding and Talairach coordinates, and also describes prediction analyses relating anticipatory activation to subsequent risky vs riskless choices. Participants are healthy volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only).

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans performing the Iowa Gambling Task, which assesses risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and provides contrasts comparing decision-making vs an active control task and choices from risky versus safe decks (risky > safe), with coordinates and cluster statistics. Participants were healthy adult males. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no clear unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-activation maps required by inclusion criterion I6. This meets exclusion criterion E6. The paper does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (contains risky > safe contrasts), I7 (healthy participants included), and I8 (results described in text/figures). However it does NOT provide the required whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6), so it cannot be included. Full text appears complete.

This study reports human fMRI data collected while participants performed a risky decision-making (loss aversion gamble) task (I4). The analyses include within-task parametric contrasts for gain-related and loss-related activation (i.e., comparisons of decision conditions by magnitude), and group-level voxelwise maps (whole-brain, cluster-corrected) are reported (I5, I6). Participant groups include substance users and HIV+ persons (eligible per review) and are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, tables, and figures (I8). The task is a risky DM paradigm (not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting/seed connectivity only), and the paper presents unmasked within-group main effects as well as group comparisons, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of human decision making under known probabilistic uncertainty (70% vs 30%) using a two-choice prediction task, meeting the meta-analysis focus on risky/uncertain decision-making. The experiment includes an active control task and reports within-task contrasts (prediction > control) for both age groups and group comparisons. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 results with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, tables, figures, and discussion, so the report is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a canonical risky decision-making task (Risky Gains). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing risky versus safe responses and punished versus non-punished outcomes, and presents both a-priori ROI and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction), with results described in text, tables, and figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and presents condition contrasts (anticipation vs. experience; gain vs. draw vs. loss; deck A/B/C/D comparisons and time-course by monetary value) rather than only task>baseline contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain activation maps and discussed with coordinates/figures. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a probability-discounting task that manipulated risk (choices between certain smaller rewards and larger probabilistic rewards). The paper reports within-task contrasts (probabilistic/risky > fixed/certain) and between-group comparisons ((IGD possible − IGD fixed) − (HC possible − HC fixed)). Analyses were conducted at the whole-brain group level using SPM5 with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster coordinates (Table 1 and figures). Participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) are acceptable per review criteria. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the content is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain analyses in healthy participants (adolescents and adults) and reports whole-brain results; however, the task is a reward-processing Card Guessing Task that the authors explicitly state is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Contrasts are reward vs. no-reward (reward receipt/consumption), not risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts. Therefore it fails the required scope for decision-making tasks in this review. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5.

This article reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary guessing task with uncertain outcomes (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying the risky decision-making domain. The study includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports task contrasts (gain > loss; feedback and reward-relevant trials versus reward-neutral control trials are modeled), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results presented in figures and tables. Participants are human (healthy young adults). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (within-task contrast comparing decision-making conditions and task vs control), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses, PET, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study acquired fMRI while human participants performed decision-making tasks that include explicit risky/uncertainty conditions (uncertainty task with specified probabilities) and a complex task combining delay and uncertainty. First-level contrasts were computed comparing each task against an active control task, and group-level, whole-brain activation maps are reported (figures and thresholded maps). Participants are healthy humans. Thus the paper provides voxelwise, group-level task-evoked fMRI results for decision-making involving risk/uncertainty. It does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not PET, contrasts are task vs control not implicit baseline). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that directly probes risky decision-making using monetary gambles (high-probability small payoff vs low-probability large payoff). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts (parametric regressors for intradimensional vs unidimensional differences; preferential choice vs judgment-based choice paired t-tests), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5; cluster-corrected results, reported peak MNI coordinates). Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Subjects are healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition and task-vs-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that investigates perceptual decision-making (categorization under sensory uncertainty). It reports within-task comparisons of decision-related conditions (radial vs concentric choices; analyses of stimuli near the category boundary/hard vs easier trials) and uses whole-brain, group-level searchlight MVPA with second-level t-tests (voxelwise maps reported; p<0.0001 cluster-threshold). The study includes full methods, results, and group whole-brain statistical analyses, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study in which human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning decision-making task (uncertain/probabilistic rewards and punishments), meeting the review’s domain (risky/ambiguous decision-making). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted in SPM5: parametric first-level regressors (learning rate, expected value, prediction error) and second-level 1-sample t tests and full-factorial ANOVAs (including comparisons across trial types: correct/wrong × rewarded/punished). These provide task-evoked whole-brain maps (not ROI-only) and within-task contrasts (via the 12-regressor model and ANOVAs), not solely task>implicit baseline contrasts. Participants and methods are fully reported. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses to examine covariance between risk level (parametric modulation of explosion probability) and brain activation, comparing post-win vs post-loss decision events. It reports voxelwise random-effects analyses (2x2 ANOVA) with whole-brain cluster correction and within-group maps, satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts (risk-level parametric effects and after-loss vs after-win comparisons). Participants are human adolescents (IGD and HCs). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face gender categorization) with manipulation of stimulus coherence (phase noise) and morphing to change difficulty. It reports within-task contrasts comparing noise-present (low coherence) versus noise-absent (higher coherence) and versus control, matching perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., low coherence > high coherence). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates (Table 1) and conjunctions; ROI analyses are supplemental but do not replace whole-brain maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study reports ROI-based fMRI analyses and forward-model reconstructions in early visual areas rather than providing a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task) and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast of the accepted forms such as hard>easy or low-coherence>high-coherence in the main fMRI experiment; coherence was fixed per subject) and I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group activation maps reported; analyses focus on selected ROIs and reconstruction performance). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) during task-based fMRI, providing within-task contrasts based on risk level (parametric 'risk level' pump regressor) and reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds). The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full text present) and reports whole-brain results in the text (with supplemental materials referenced). Although the paper also presents resting-state connectivity analyses, it also provides task-evoked whole-brain contrasts appropriate for risky decision-making (high-risk > low-risk type parametric contrast). Participant sample (nicotine-dependent smokers) is an allowed population. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, or only connectivity without task maps) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making task fMRI and whole-brain reporting.

This longitudinal fMRI study used the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task and reports a risky vs. safe selection contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AFNI 3dANOVA3) with cluster correction and results reported in tables/figures (Table 2, Figures). Participants include adolescents who became binge drinkers and matched controls (acceptable participant groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no baseline-only contrasts, not PET, task is risky-DM, reports whole-brain results beyond ROIs, not only connectivity, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of decision-making under maximum uncertainty (ambiguous DM) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports of coordinates, but the critical decision-making contrasts are 50% probability condition > implicit baseline (task > implicit baseline). The paper does not report condition-versus-condition contrasts of uncertainty (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty) or task > active control task. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts vs implicit baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant groups), I8 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control decision-making contrast). Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that directly examines perceptual decision-making (emotion vs. gender categorizations of faces). It reports condition-vs-control contrasts (emotion > control, gender > control) and direct decision-condition contrasts (emotion > gender and vice versa), meeting the required perceptual-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise maps with corrected cluster thresholds and reported activation coordinates/tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and contrasts are against an active control task rather than implicit baseline).

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans using a gambling task that manipulates reward uncertainty (uncertain, probable, certain) during decision-making, i.e., a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., uncertain wins > probable wins; probable wins > probable losses) and examines outcome effects (wins vs losses). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (t-to-z maps, exploratory whole-brain contrasts) and ROI definitions derived from whole-brain contrasts. Participants were healthy adults. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous DM), I5 (condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only task>rest contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete.

The study uses fMRI and reports whole-brain, group-level parametric maps of neural activity related to perceived social risk during purchase decisions. However, the task probes social risk / social judgment (anticipated disapproval) in consumer choices rather than risky decision-making defined as decisions involving objective or probabilistic risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. Therefore it reflects social/moral decision-making, not the risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision types targeted by the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a perceptual target-detection task with morphed stimuli that manipulated ambiguity and perceptual similarity. It reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., morph1 vs. target) and uses similarity and ambiguity regressors to predict BOLD, including whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FDR correction; coordinates and activation maps are reported. Participants are human healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets criteria for an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), provides condition-wise contrasts (I5), reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results/maps (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and provides whole-brain results/coordinates in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment (BART) involving risky decision making in human participants, with within-task contrasts distinguishing risky versus safe choices and parametric modulators (e.g., ChooseInflate*P(explode), ChooseWin*P(explode)) and planned contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (with FDR and cluster correction) including coordinate tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>rest-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic multi-cue decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty and time pressure. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (parametric modulation by subjective and objective sum of evidence, phase contrasts HighP>LowP, conjunctions) with corrected voxelwise cluster results and tables of clusters. Task contrasts compare decision conditions (low vs high time pressure) and parametric contrasts indexing uncertainty/evidence (high vs low SoE), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults using a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task (uncertain outcomes across 80/20, 70/30, 60/40 pairs). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Crucially, they include parametric contrasts indexing unsigned prediction error (absolute PE) and its overlap with post-error slowing (i.e., brain activity increasing with surprise/uncertainty), which corresponds to a high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty type contrast relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, no ROI-only, not task>rest only, and not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans during a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) with explicit risky vs. cautious choices and decision-periods (I4). It uses an active control condition (Directed Trials) and reports the key contrast (Decision Trial – Directed Trial) and separate analyses for risky vs. cautious deliberation, satisfying the allowed decision>control and within-task contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM8 maps with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster/tables/figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements (I6, I8). Participant groups include adolescents with conduct/substance problems and matched comparisons, which are acceptable per eligibility (I7). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task probing cognitive flexibility and feedback processing, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and figures/tables (I6, I8) and includes healthy human participants (I7), it does not employ an accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm or contrasts (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguous', 'hard > easy'). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans using a risky decision-making task (modified Balloon Analog Risk Task) with both active (choice) and passive (no-choice) conditions. It includes within- and between-task contrasts (e.g., active risk vs. passive risk; active inflation vs. passive inflation; active loss vs. passive loss) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLM results (normalized to MNI space, reported with whole-brain FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster tables), and results are presented in figures and tables. Participants are healthy humans. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the report is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study acquired fMRI while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving decisions under probabilistic (uncertain) outcomes. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses of task-evoked signals (model-derived reward prediction error (RPE) parametric modulators) with family-wise error correction, and conducted within-task comparisons (RPE modulation; exploratory binning of negative/neutral/positive RPEs) and group comparisons. The task constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (probabilistic/ambiguous learning), and the contrasts (parametric RPE effect and binned RPE comparisons) are within-task decision-related contrasts that are reported at the whole-brain group level. Participants are human and within accepted age range. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, not resting-state-only, empirical fMRI with whole-brain maps). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an fMRI study in humans that used a lottery decision task manipulating reward probabilities (prior and likelihood) and sample-size (uncertainty) during choices between lotteries. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (GLMs) with corrected statistical maps and coordinates (e.g., mPFC, striatum, occipital cortex) and contrasts/parametric effects comparing decision conditions (e.g., sample-size conditions, parametric regressors for prior/likelihood/posterior and likelihood uncertainty). Participants were healthy adults. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons across conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study includes an fMRI experiment in human participants that manipulated decision difficulty via manual bistability (ambiguous posture selection) and modeled a parametric predictor of bistability (a within-task decision-making contrast analogous to hard>easy). The analysis produced group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps of the parametric effect, reported in text/tables/figures. Participants were healthy adults. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, not only baseline contrasts). Hence it meets inclusion criteria for perceptual/ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Gain vs Loss trials) during whole-brain BOLD acquisition. The authors model a trial-by-trial parametric regressor (‘Gamble Risk’) and report within-task contrasts (risk parametric effects, Valence: Gain > Loss comparisons and related interactions), as well as ON vs OFF medication and group interactions. Imaging analyses are whole-brain (SPM5) with FDR correction and results are described in the text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, not a review). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides whole-brain contrasts suitable for meta-analysis.

This study reports fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion), with detailed methods and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) present — full text appears complete. The authors report group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses: (1) univariate parametric contrasts relating BOLD to motion coherence (including low-coherence > high-coherence effects), and (2) whole-brain searchlight multivariate classification with group repeated-measures ANOVA and reported peak coordinates/figures. These provide condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual DM (e.g., low coherence vs high coherence) and whole-brain, group-level statistical maps reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This single-case study reports task-based fMRI during decision-making and reports a condition contrast (A>B) and whole-brain voxelwise results, but it is a single-subject (n=1) study rather than a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Inclusion criterion I6 requires group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) maps; that criterion is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous DM), I5 (explicit condition contrast A>B, task>control), I7 (participant group is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis are triggered. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I6 is not met), the study must be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic decision-making task that manipulates risk. The authors modelled trial-by-trial risk prediction and used GLM parametric regressors to produce group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster- and voxel-level corrected) identifying regions correlating with risk prediction; they report and correlate these maps with behavior and personality. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation indexing risk prediction across conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) with explicit contrasts between risky decision trials (DecBa) and an active control/baseline directed trial (DirBa) for decision, win, and loss periods. The analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise maps (SPM) reported with cluster- and voxel-level corrections and coordinates. Participants include clinical (ASD) and control groups (adolescents), which are acceptable. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and provides coordinate-based results and figures. Relevant contrasts include risk-related contrasts (bad > good deck; ‘risk effect’) and framed-message versus control comparisons (heightened-risk effect), which meet the accepted forms for risky decision-making contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an event-related gambling (guessing) task that manipulates uncertainty/risk during the anticipation phase. It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Anticipation $4 vs No-change; Ant $4–No-ch $4 and Ant 50c–No-ch 50c) rather than task>rest, satisfying risky/ambiguous decision contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8, voxelwise thresholding with cluster reporting) with results presented as clusters/coordinates and parameter estimates. Participants are healthy humans in a crossover design. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in humans that explicitly examined risky decision-making using a lottery choice task (risk manipulated via coefficient of variation). The fMRI analysis included a group-level whole-brain analysis testing how CV for chosen gambles modulated BOLD during the decision phase (reporting higher vs lower risk effects in bilateral anterior insula with FWE correction), which constitutes condition-vs-condition/riskier>safer contrasts (parametric modulation). Participants are human adolescents (eligible by I7). Whole-brain results and coordinates/ROIs are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and whole-brain group-level contrasts.

This study used task-based fMRI in human participants performing an anticipation task with an 'uncertain event' versus 'certain reward' contrast (meets I4 and I5). Participant sample and reporting (healthy adults) are acceptable (meets I7), and peak coordinates are reported (meets I8). However, the reported analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction (SVC) within those regions; there is no evidence of an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map. Because the paper reports only ROI-based voxel searches/SVC without whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) during scanning, and it reports the critical contrast of risky > safe choices. The authors performed group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (one-sample t-tests on contrast images, with cluster correction) and report coordinates and ROI results; thus whole-brain task-evoked maps are available. Participant groups (suicide attempters, affective controls, healthy controls) are acceptable under the review’s participant inclusions. The contrasts and task directly map onto the meta-analysis objective of risky decision-making. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete (includes methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4), reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with cluster-level FWE correction (I6), included an eligible participant sample (I7), and presented whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). However, it does not report any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Instead, the fMRI analysis used model-derived parametric modulators for reward prediction errors (RPEcue and RPEoutcome) and between-group comparisons of those parametric effects; no within-task contrast of risky vs safe or ambiguous vs non-ambiguous (I5) is provided. Because I5 is not met, the study does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none of the explicit exclusion items (e.g., PET only, ROI-only) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans using a near-threshold pain-detection paradigm (perceptual decision-making). The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (pain vs no pain; high threat vs low threat; interaction contrasts) relevant to perceptual decision-making, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates. Results include anticipation and stimulation contrasts and whole-brain SPM analyses. The task is a perceptual decision task (detection/classification of stimulus as painful vs nonpainful), satisfying the perceptual-DM domain. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used fMRI in human participants performing a risky lottery task (I4) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I6) with results described in the text and figures (I8), it does not provide at least one accepted risky-decision contrast as required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, or experimental risk task > control task). The reported fMRI contrasts focus on social versus private contexts and outcome valence (social gain/loss) and connectivity, not on contrasts that isolate risk level or task-versus-control risk activity. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study (wheel-of-fortune risky decision task) meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI in humans), I5 (risky > safe contrast: 10/30 vs 70/90), and I7 (healthy participant groups). However, the primary neuroimaging analysis was restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and reported ROI peak coordinates; the paper does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I6. Because the report presents only ROI-limited results (no whole-brain voxelwise maps), it falls under exclusion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group map) and I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables—no qualifying whole-brain results were provided). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with participants scanned during decisions. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Risk vs. No-Risk; Risk > No-Risk and No-Risk > Risk) that match admissible risky-DM contrasts (risk > certainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME) are reported with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of whole-brain activation coordinates and contrasts of interest for the meta-analysis.

Although this study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, the analyses reported and emphasized in the paper are limited to the feedback/outcome phase (Win vs. No Win). The meta-analysis requires at least one contrast that compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty) or a decision-making task vs an active control (I5). This study does not report or focus on any decision-phase contrasts of risk vs. safe (selection/choice-phase contrasts); instead the primary contrast is reward receipt vs reward absence, which is an outcome/feedback contrast rather than a decision-making contrast of interest. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of risky economic decision-making (mixed lotteries) conducted in human participants (MDD and healthy controls), satisfying I4. The analysis includes condition-wise parametric modulators for gains and losses and directly contrasts gain versus loss coding (gains > losses and losses > gains) and group interactions, satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results and coordinates (including whole-brain and ROI-corrected findings, supplementary tables/figures) meeting I6 and I8. Participant groups (MDD and HC) are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), does not use only baseline contrasts (it uses condition contrasts, so E3 not met), reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only, E6), is not connectivity/resting-only (E7), includes within-group task effects (E8), and is empirical (not E9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human older adults performing a lottery choice task that manipulates risk via probabilities and magnitudes (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts using parametric modulators of expected value (EV) and group-level voxelwise analyses identifying positive and negative EV sensitivity, age and risk-preference effects, and feedback-related contrasts; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps with peak-voxel tables and figures. These analyses satisfy the requirement for condition-vs-condition/task contrasts (e.g., sensitivity to high vs low EV/riskier vs surer) and provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation evidence. The task and sample fall within eligible participant groups. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probability (risk) discounting task (probabilistic rewards) and a delay discounting task. The probability discounting task constitutes a risky decision-making paradigm. The main reported contrasts include free vs. forced choice (decision vs. an active, matched control), meeting the requirement for a task-versus-control contrast. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM; coordinates and FWE-corrected results reported), and results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participants include clinical and non-clinical groups (allowed). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (Exclusion E5). The task is a serial reaction time sequential prediction task, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm, and it does not report contrasts of the forms required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Satisfies other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses are reported (I6), participant sample is acceptable (I7), and whole-brain results/coordinates are provided in supplementary tables (I8). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (appropriate decision-making contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary material).

This is an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky mixed-lottery decision-making task (lottery choice task) with within-task contrasts and parametric modulation of probability and magnitude. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and model-based one-sample tests), thresholding, and ROI analyses derived from whole-brain results. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and condition-versus-condition/parametric contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Participants are healthy human adults; results include within-group task effects and between-group (age) interactions. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision task (reporting painful vs. non-painful detection), meeting the review's perceptual-DM definition. The paper reports condition-wise GLM contrasts (pain vs. no pain during anticipation and stimulation) and whole-brain group-level analyses. It additionally provides whole-brain MVPA results including FWE-corrected voxelwise maps and group-level permutation tests. Participants are human and results are presented in standard whole-brain formats. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting/connectivity-only; not ROI-only; contrasts are condition-vs-condition, not baseline-only). Full text appears complete.

The manuscript reports an fMRI experiment in which human subjects made risky and ambiguous choices (I4 satisfied) and models condition-specific parametric regressors for risk and ambiguity (within-task contrasts; I5 satisfied). Participant sampling is acceptable (human subjects; I7 satisfied). However, the paper is a methods-oriented JoVE article that presents representative single-subject activation maps and descriptions of the analysis pipeline; it does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required by the review (I6 NOT met). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not PET, and not task>rest only). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks clearly reported group-level whole-brain results.

This is a human fMRI study in which cocaine-dependent participants performed a Paper-Scissors-Rock reinforcement-learning task during fMRI. The task manipulates uncertainty/probability (preferred 90%, even 50%, worst 10%) and the authors model decision-phase contrasts of early (high uncertainty/learning) versus late (low uncertainty/execution) trials, which maps onto an ambiguous-DM contrast (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI GLM, AlphaSim correction) with cluster tables and Talairach coordinates. Participants are a substance-using clinical sample (acceptable). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task, with analyses linking neural activation to increasing risk (balloon size/adjusted pumps). It provides a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map (correlation maps transformed to z-scores and t-tested at group level) and reports peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The neural contrast is a within-task parametric modulation of risk level (effectively high-risk > low-risk), satisfying the required decision-making contrast forms. Participants include adolescents with TBI and healthy controls (eligible sample types). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and within-task whole-brain effects are reported).
