Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (difference judgment) during scanning and reports task-versus-control contrasts (judgment > passive viewing/blank) and within-task contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects) are reported, with coordinates and figures (Talairach coordinates, Table 1, and group maps). The task falls squarely within perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only rest contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (direction-of-motion discrimination) with two coherence levels. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and condition-versus-condition contrasts (high-coherence vs low-coherence; conjunction analyses across response modalities), and provides coordinates and statistical maps. The methods and results include mixed-effects whole-brain GLM analyses and thresholded Z-statistic images, satisfying the review’s requirements for task-evoked whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing an explicit risky decision-making gambling task with explicit probabilities and reward/punishment conditions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses and contrasts of task conditions against a neutral control (reward>neutral, loss>neutral), satisfying the required task-versus-control contrast form. Whole-brain results are reported (tables/coordinates) and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full article contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses a delay discounting / intertemporal choice task (delay discounting, Intertemporal Choice Task), which falls outside the review scope. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — delay discounting/intertemporal choice excluded) is met. The paper does report whole-brain, group-level fMRI activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (hard>easy, hard>no, easy>no), so inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) are satisfied. However I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is not satisfied, and I5 (contrasts appropriate to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not applicable for the review domains. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual detection decision-making task (animal detection) and reports within-task condition contrasts (Pos > Neut-P and Neg > Neut-N) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters, coordinates provided) alongside ROI analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the listed exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (guesses about a briefly flashed stimulus) with a scanner-based phase manipulating uncertainty and social vs individual information. The authors report group-level, whole-brain (SPM8 random-effects) analyses with cluster FWE correction and local maxima coordinates, and they present condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., I:I vs integration conditions; S:S > I:S). These contrasts constitute within-task condition comparisons relevant to perceptual decision-making under uncertainty. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition vs condition decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task that manipulates outcome uncertainty (risk/ambiguity). The primary imaging contrasts compare punished (probabilistic error) versus rewarded correct responses (a within-task condition-versus-condition contrast relevant to decision-making under uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM, cluster-level FWE correction) with results reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Participant groups (ADHD persisters/remitters and matched controls) are acceptable per eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI-only analyses, only connectivity, only PET, or only task>baseline contrasts — it reports whole-brain task activation and within-group contrasts. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly, include the study.

This study reports an fMRI investigation in humans performing a decision-making task that manipulated uncertainty (odd–even–pass task: uncertain > certain). It includes a clear decision-making contrast (uncertain > certain, matching ambiguous/risky DM), reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reported activations/coordinates, and includes both clinical (IGD) and healthy control groups. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and includes whole-brain task maps).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a Risky-Gains decision-making task (risky vs safe choices). The manuscript includes within-subject contrasts comparing risky > safe and risky > punished conditions, and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with threshold/cluster correction and Talairach normalization, with coordinates and figures. Personality correlations are ancillary but do not affect eligibility. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, voxelwise analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging results with tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that directly examines neural responses to risk and ambiguity in a task contrast relevant to decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) SPM analyses with second-level RFX contrasts including ambiguity > risk and ambiguity > ignorance, and provides tables/figures of coordinates and clusters. The experimental manipulation and reported contrasts match the meta-analysis inclusion forms (e.g., "ambiguity > ignorance"). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and includes within-group whole-brain task contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house discrimination near threshold). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., HF > FH, FFhc > HHhc), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected results, coordinates and figures). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures. The full text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents that used a risky decision-making task (the Social Analogue Risk Task) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. The authors modeled knock, cash-out, and slam events and used a parametric modulator (cash-out PM) indexing increasing risk (number of knocks) and conducted whole-brain group analyses (including cluster-corrected results). Results (main effects and regressions) are reported across the whole brain in the text and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast via parametric modulation of risk/cash-out), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (human adolescent sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task with stochastic rewards (decision-making under uncertainty/risk). It includes within-task contrasts and model-based regressors that compare decision conditions (e.g., switch > stay, prior-correct/value contrasts, and direct model comparisons state-based vs RL). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates and thresholding, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than task>implicit baseline). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/uncertain decision-making.

This study reports whole-brain fMRI collected while human participants performed a probabilistic (uncertainty-manipulated) reinforcement learning task with monetary outcomes (50%, 69%, 100% predictability). The authors report voxelwise, group-level contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (predictability-related contrasts: 100%<69%<50%, within-group and between-group comparisons) with whole-brain statistical maps and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task with uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts across uncertainty levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probability-discounting risky choice task during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts indexing decision variables (subjective value, decision conflict) and presents decision-conflict effects (equivalent to hard > easy) and value-related contrasts (meets I5). Analyses were conducted and reported at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with thresholds and clusters reported (meets I6). Participants are healthy adult males (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures (meets I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient detail is present to assess eligibility. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving game). It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Pass > Crash), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) with reported peak coordinates. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion). It reports condition contrasts of interest (low coherence > high coherence), matching the perceptual-DM contrast types in I5. Authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses and present group maps/statistics (permutation testing and cluster correction), satisfying I6. Participants are healthy adults (I7). Results and whole-brain maps are reported in the main text and figures (I8). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This fMRI study used the weather prediction probabilistic category-learning task (prediction > perceptual-motor baseline), so it involves decision-making under uncertainty and includes an active task>control contrast (I4 and I5). Participants are human and groups are acceptable (I7), and whole-brain results are described in the text/figures (I8). However, the authors performed an ROI-based SPM factorial ANOVA (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROI masks from the AAL library) and report only ROI-focused activation results. They did not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map; thus the study reports only ROI analyses and lacks whole-brain voxelwise task maps (violates I6) and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic classification (category learning) task with informational feedback, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined for this meta-analysis. It does not report any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). It does, however, report group-level whole-brain analyses and includes healthy participants. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are met, but I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E5 (task not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) applies.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an ambiguous decision-making task (valence judgments of sounds with manipulated consonance/dissonance). Relevant contrasts compare ambiguous vs less-ambiguous conditions (intermediate dissonance > consonance; strong > intermediate), meeting the required condition-vs-condition contrasts for ambiguous-DM. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests) are reported, with cluster and voxel-level thresholding and coordinates presented. Participants are healthy human adults. Results and coordinates are reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-task contrasts rather than only task>rest). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

While the study acquired simultaneous EEG–fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (I6) with healthy participants (I7) and whole-brain results/tables described in the text (I8), it does not present any eligible decision-making contrast as required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, or hard>easy). The reported analyses focus on parametric regressors (signed and absolute RPEs), EEG-informed fMRI associations, and DCM rather than contrasts comparing decision conditions or a task vs active control. Therefore I5 is not met and the study is excluded.

This fMRI study tested risky decision-making (child-friendly cake gambling task) during scanning with healthy human participants, reporting contrasts comparing decision conditions (high-risk > low-risk; negative > positive feedback). It includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain section, tables of activations and figures) and reports coordinates and ROI results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. All inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no contrasts only versus baseline, no PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants making risk-related decisions in driving (urgent braking vs. risk evaluation). It reports within-task condition contrasts (urgent > evaluative and vice versa) that are directly relevant to risky decision-making, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12, AlphaSim correction) and reports cluster coordinates/tables and figures. The tasks constitute risky decision-making (braking to avoid hazards), satisfying the meta-analysis scope. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>baseline only), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and the paper is empirical. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing life–death framing tasks (risky decision-making). It reports within-task contrasts comparing positive (gain) vs negative (loss) framing and large vs small group contexts (condition vs condition), with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of MNI coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and whole-brain results are reported (Table 2, figures). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI while participants performed perceptual decision-making tasks (spatial comparison and shape comparison), with active baseline target-detection trials and contrasts of interest (spatial comparison > baseline; within- vs between-image comparisons). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise activation and contrasts are reported in the text and figures. Participants were healthy adults. Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4, I5) and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps at the group level (I6). Reporting in figures/text meets I8, and participant population is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting-state/ROI-only; contrasts are against an active control rather than implicit baseline). Full text appears complete.

Excluded (E5): The task is probabilistic association learning (Weather Prediction Task), a learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy controls and schizophrenia patients), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) is not satisfied because the WPT is an associative learning task rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm; I5 (required decision-making contrasts) is not satisfied in the sense required by the review (risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy, or analogous uncertainty/risk contrasts). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses an fMRI trust/reciprocity (social) task and contrasts human versus computer interaction; this is social decision-making rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy; primary contrast is human>computer). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (I6) and includes participant groups that are acceptable for the review (patients and controls; I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/tables (I8). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning/reward-learning paradigm and the reported contrasts are feedback-related (negative vs positive feedback; final reversal vs reversal error; final reversal error vs correct), not the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrasts). It also does not unambiguously meet I4 as a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making manipulation per the meta-analysis definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are directly triggered, but because not all inclusion criteria are met (notably I5 and I4), the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulated risk and ambiguity during a decision-making task (bowling-ball gambles) and acquired BOLD images during task performance. The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (ambiguous > nonambiguous; parametric effect of second-order entropy; other contrasts related to outcome range and risk probability) rather than task>rest, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 RFX one-sample t tests with cluster- and voxel-level corrections) with tables/figures of results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in human smokers using the Wheel of Fortune, a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task. The paper reports task-versus-control contrasts (money > control) during selection and anticipation phases and win>no-win during outcome, modeled and reported at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables/figures). Participant group (nicotine-dependent smokers) is acceptable. Reporting includes coordinates, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are against an active control (not implicit baseline), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts without within-task effects. Full text is complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (decision-making under ambiguity/risk) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. It includes within-task condition contrasts (disadvantageous > advantageous, advantageous > disadvantageous; win > loss; EV-modulated outcome contrasts) satisfying condition-versus-condition contrast requirements. The authors ran whole-brain permutation-based group analyses and report clusterwise results and coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participant group (healthy adult males) is acceptable. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental material noted but core article content present). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (framing task) with choices between a sure option and a gamble, satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision types (e.g., sure vs gamble within gain/loss frames and the framing-effect contrast [(Gsure + Lgamble) − (Lsure + Ggamble)]), satisfying I5. Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise maps (with thresholding and reported peak coordinates), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants were healthy volunteers (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so is complete. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task is a risky decision-making task. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans that used two-choice perceptual decision-making tasks (numerical and verbal) during scanning, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses linking task activation to behavioral parameters. The paper reports between-task comparisons (numerical vs. verbal) and task-related contrasts, and performs whole-brain random-effects analyses and multiple-regression voxelwise maps (thresholded and reported with coordinates). The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only baseline contrasts without task-vs-task comparisons) are met. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This fMRI study (beads/JTC probabilistic inference) involved human participants performing a decision-making task (I4) and included an active control condition (control blocks) allowing task-versus-control comparisons (I5). Participants were healthy adults (I7) and results are described in the full text (I8). However, the analyses are ROI- and multivariate-pattern-based (Harvard-Oxford masks, voxel-selection within ROI masks) and the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; rather, results focus on ROI statistics and selected-voxel patterns. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Because failing any required inclusion criterion and meeting E6 mandates exclusion, I exclude this paper from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a risky decision-making task (modified Lane risk-taking task) performed during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices and feedback conditions (risky > safe; win > safe; loss > safe), and both within-condition and condition-by-task interactions (alcohol vs placebo). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded with cluster correction; results are reported with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy social drinkers. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (subjects bluffing in a domino game) and includes condition contrasts (nonmatch [risky] vs match [safe]) with healthy human participants. However, MRI acquisition used a small number of slices centered on the amygdala (partial brain coverage) and analyses focus on anatomically defined ROI and small-volume/group GLMs restricted to the amygdala; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported. Therefore the study does not provide whole-brain results required for inclusion and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only / no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (ambiguous cue conditioning) with explicit choices (obtain reward vs avoid punishment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) including condition contrasts (positive tone vs negative tone) and parametric modulations across tones (linear and quadratic effects indexing valence generalization and ambiguity). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and tables with cluster-level FWE correction. Participants and task fall squarely within the ambiguous decision-making domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET-only, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study of causal/one-shot learning but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (human participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study in healthy adults performing a card gambling task manipulating risk (six risk levels). The analysis included within-task contrasts across risk levels (e.g., low-risk vs high-risk; regressors for each risk level; control > ketanserin contrasts for low-risk negative outcomes) meeting the risky-DM contrast formats. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM5 with FWE cluster correction and coordinates reported. Thus the study satisfies: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts comparing risk levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than only task>baseline, modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky decision-making (not an excluded decision type), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task activation maps (not only connectivity or only between-group contrasts) are provided. Full text is complete and includes methods, results and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of approach–avoidance decisions under probabilistic threat (risky decision-making) that reports condition-wise contrasts across CS threat levels and provides coordinates/tables of activations. It thus satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (within-task condition comparisons using contrasts across threat levels/quadratic effects and baseline trials) and I8 (results reported in figures/tables). However, the second-level fMRI analyses were restricted to an a priori ROI mask with small-volume correction rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis. The paper does not report unmasked whole-brain task-evoked maps, so it fails I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a decision-making task manipulating uncertainty (certain vs uncertain trials). The authors report a within-task contrast (uncertain > certain) that maps ambiguity-related activation and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain thresholds) with results described in text, tables, and figures. Participants include clinical (alcoholic) and healthy groups, both acceptable. The task and contrasts directly match ambiguous decision-making criteria (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not only connectivity, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This fMRI study uses an intertemporal choice (delay discounting) task (temporal discounting / Intertemporal Choice Task). The meta-analysis explicitly excludes delay discounting/intertemporal choice tasks (Exclusion E5). The paper does include group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and condition-vs-control contrasts (satisfying I6 and I8), and participant groups are acceptable (I7). However it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4 not met) and therefore does not provide the eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts required (I5 not met). Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that used a probabilistic choice task (participants chose higher vs lower than 5 for cues with 85% vs 65% predictive probabilities). The task involves decision-making under differing levels of uncertainty (easy = low uncertainty; hard = high uncertainty), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM statistical maps and coordinates (random-effects SPMs) with contrasts that include cue difficulty (easy > hard / high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and learning-type contrasts. Thus the study provides within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts mapping onto ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty), meets whole-brain reporting, and includes appropriate participant sampling. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making under uncertainty), I5 (condition contrast: hard vs easy/high uncertainty vs low uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (results reported with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion rationale: The study employed fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (a decision-making paradigm), but the reported primary contrasts are outcome valence contrasts (reward > punishment) and positive>neutral picture viewing, not contrasts that manipulate or compare levels of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty as required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task/contrast does not match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing a decision-making task — probabilistic reversal learning), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (required decision-making contrast comparing risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty was not provided). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI and whole-brain group analyses during a probabilistic reversal learning task, but the task is a reinforcement/reversal-learning paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The reported contrasts focus on negative vs positive feedback, reversal errors, and history effects (e.g., FINREVERR vs REVERR, NEG+2 vs NEG+0), not on risk (e.g., risky>safe), ambiguity (e.g., ambiguous>non-ambiguous), or perceptual difficulty (e.g., hard>easy) contrasts required by I5. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task not in targeted DM categories). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps present), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM per the protocol) and I5 (no qualifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates free hand choice (Choice vs Instruct) and hand-specific motor planning, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and clearly describes results in the text, but it does not contain any of the required contrast forms for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual) and I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps) and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text). Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (BART) during scanning, with appropriate within-task contrasts and task-vs-control contrasts (PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, PumpsAvg > ControlAvg). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster correction and peak coordinates; both within-group and between-group effects are presented. Participants (young smokers and nonsmokers) are within allowable groups. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice task (judge stimulus as more speech vs more non-speech). The experiment manipulated stimulus ambiguity/difficulty (pure vs blended stimuli) and modeledcondition-wise BOLD responses (Speech: speech vs non-speech; Correctness; Time), and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates. Thus it provides within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making and reports whole-brain group activation maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic decision-making (beads/JTC) task that manipulates uncertainty. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (with FWE correction) as well as ROI results, and includes contrasts comparing the decision task to an active control task (JTC blocks > control blocks) and event-related contrasts (last fish > preceding fish) that index decision-making under uncertainty. Participants are healthy humans. Results are reported with coordinates and whole-brain statistical inference. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not only ROI; not resting-state/connectivity-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study meets the review’s inclusion criteria: (I4) it collected fMRI data while human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (BART); (I5) it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (Pumps > Control (color pumps vs. white control pumps), Cash Outs contrasts); (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates; (I7) participant group (healthy adolescents from Mexican backgrounds) is acceptable; (I8) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts include task-versus-control rather than only implicit baseline. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore include for meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This is an empirical concurrent TMS-fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (visual detection) task. The paper reports within-task, decision-related contrasts (misses vs. hits; misses vs. correct rejections) and tests interactions with TMS, which are valid decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (permutation-based cluster correction across the whole brain) and results are reported in the text, figures and tables. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion met: E5 - the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) task focused on contingency learning and prediction-error signaling, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses with reported coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds), I7 (participant sample falls within acceptable groups/age range), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not classified as a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm per the review definitions), I5 (the reported contrasts—punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses—are within a reversal-learning framework and do not match the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (Cups task) with an explicit risky>safe contrast (I4, I5). Participants are humans and age range fits (I7), and results/coordinates are reported in detail (I8). However, the paper's reported group-level task activation results for the risky>safe contrast were analyzed/thresholded within an a priori anterior insula ROI rather than presented as a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. While the study does report whole-brain PPI (connectivity) results, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task activation map for the decision contrast, so it effectively reports ROI-only task activation (violates inclusion I6) and thus meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain task results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a two-choice prediction task manipulating error rates (20%, 50%, 80%), which operationalizes risky and ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of significant clusters/coordinates and corrected thresholds. Analyses included comparisons across error-rate conditions and interoception states (e.g., effects during 80% punishment vs other conditions and Group x ER x Interoception interactions), providing within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts rather than only task>implicit-baseline contrasts. Participant groups include methamphetamine users and healthy controls, which is acceptable. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply based on the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is an ultimatum/dictator social fairness task (decision to punish/accept unfair offers), which is social/economic decision-making, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts reported: UG (unfair–fair) and UG−DG contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) — the task does not involve risk/uncertainty or perceptual difficulty as defined by the review. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) administered in the scanner. It reports within-task condition contrasts including Go > Stop (risky > safe) and Good > Bad outcomes (i.e., risk vs safety and positive vs negative outcomes), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results, tables, and NeuroVault uploads), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are a human sample (adolescents) and thus acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts rather than only task>rest, and is an original empirical fMRI activation study. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore this study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (3D heading discrimination) with explicit contrasts comparing decision difficulty (EASY vs HARD) across two stimulus manipulations (COH and FOE). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects t-maps, conjunction analysis) are reported with thresholding and coordinates; results are presented in text, figures, and ROI follow-up. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates none of the listed exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence) with response-signal manipulation. The analyses include condition-wise (motion coherence × duration) GLMs, parametric contrasts for motion coherence (equivalent to 'low coherence > high coherence' / 'hard > easy'), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (spatial maps normalized to MNI) and ICA-derived whole-brain components. Results are reported at the group level with spatial maps and ROIs; whole-text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to perceptual DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a monetary probability task (cues with 0,25,50,75,100% chance) that manipulates decision-making under risk/uncertainty. The authors report within-subject condition contrasts (linear contrasts across five expectation conditions and outcome regressors contrasting positive vs negative prediction error), computed at the group (second) level with voxelwise SPM analyses and whole-brain FWE correction. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are described in text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making paradigm). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing high-risk (decks A/B) versus low-risk (decks C/D) selections (i.e., high-risk > low-risk), and present group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (FSL group analysis, MNI registration, Z-thresholding and cluster correction). Participant groups (pathological gamblers and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only).

This is an fMRI study in human participants that explicitly investigates perceptual decision-making under high vs low visibility. It contains a whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analysis (searchlight decoding and random-effects GLM) comparing decision conditions (low visibility/guessing vs high visibility/perceptual) analogous to hard>easy or low-coherence>high-coherence contrasts. Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures. Participants meet eligibility, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only) are violated. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision making (object recognition) with human participants. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures mixed-effects ANOVA), contrasts across decision conditions (recognition time TR3–7, comparisons of correct vs. TR8, and static vs. shuffle trials), and presents whole-brain maps and ROI coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making card gambling task (meets I4). It reports explicit condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (risk scaled linear contrast; high-risk wins > low-risk wins) matching accepted risky-DM contrast forms (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level maps with reported cluster coordinates and corrected p-values (meets I6). Participants are healthy humans (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and clearly described (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are violated: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not only task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results provided, not ROI/ connectivity-only, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains), and reports a direct risky > safe contrast (risky vs. safe choices). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps (paired t-tests, voxel-wise correlations) with reported coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. Participant group (adolescents with excess weight) is eligible. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI/connectivity, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that includes probabilistic (risky) decision trials and directly contrasts probabilistic versus intertemporal valuation (reports R>D and D>R contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results with cluster-corrected maps and tabulated local maxima, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Although the task also includes intertemporal (delay) trials (which alone would be excluded), the presence of risky/probabilistic trials and explicit risk versus delay contrasts makes the study relevant to risky decision-making. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

Full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making card prediction task manipulating outcome uncertainty (uncertain vs. certain). The paper includes an explicit Uncertain > Certain (Uncertain–Certain action selection) contrast, computed voxelwise and tested at the group level with whole-brain analyses and cluster correction; significant clusters and coordinates are reported in Table 2. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are acceptable per review scope. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI study of ambiguous/risky decision-making with a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast and reported coordinates.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a monetary gambling task (risky decision-making) and therefore directly addresses the review objective. It includes within-task contrasts comparing levels of risk (a linear gambling-risk contrast and high-risk > low-risk outcome contrasts), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (second-level SPM8 ANOVA) with reported cluster results and MNI coordinates and FWE correction; ROI-restricted corrections were also used but whole-brain results are present. Participant sample (healthy twins at familial risk) is an allowed subject group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=23) who performed a probability-learning and gamble-choice task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., active decision phase > control phase; parametric modulation by stimulus probability, outcome and choice entropy) and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates, thresholds, and corrections (FDR/FWE). Methods, results, and statistics for whole-brain maps are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts such as active > control and parametric contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not ROI-only, not rest-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E5 met: the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm probing cognitive flexibility, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision/choice task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the study does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts focus on phase (acquisition vs reversal) and accuracy (correct win vs incorrect loss) and diagnostic group interactions rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrast types and must be excluded.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy humans performing an explicit risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains Task). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., +80 vs +40 high-risk > low-risk, and regressors for safe [20] vs risky [40/80]) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (LME) with cluster-corrected results and tables of coordinates. Results are presented in the main text/tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts: high-risk>low-risk and safe vs risky regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling (Blackjack) task that manipulates risk. It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (e.g., high-risk hits > low-risk hits; low-risk sits > high-risk sits) matching risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses used group-level, random-effects, voxelwise statistics and report Talairach coordinates and whole-brain/exploratory activations (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are an eligible group (healthy students). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, task>rest contrasts only) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This study meets the meta-analysis requirements: it acquired fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) and reports condition-wise contrasts (risky vs safe). Analyses were voxel-wise and a whole-brain analysis of group-by-decision effects is reported (supplementary figure/table), with coordinates and cluster results provided. Participants are a qualifying group (substance-using methamphetamine-dependent individuals). Results include task-evoked, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (risk>safe / risky–safe) and reported AUC/ROC for predictive value. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-task contrasts). Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but main article content is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that experimentally manipulated decision difficulty and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making. The task required subjects to decide whether a presented probe color matched one or more memorized colors; sample–probe similarity (match, similar non-match, dissimilar non-match) and memory load (1 vs 3 items) produced condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., similarity main effect; high vs low load), which map onto perceptual decision-making contrasts (hard > easy). Analyses were whole-brain SPM random-effects ANOVAs with FDR correction and peak coordinates/tables reported. No exclusion criteria were triggered: contrasts are not baseline-only, the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the task fits within the perceptual decision-making domain as argued by the authors. Full text is complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house discrimination with parametrically varied noise). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing easier (suprathreshold) vs harder (perithreshold) perceptual decisions (e.g., easier > harder), and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with thresholded Z-statistic maps. Results and coordinates are reported in main text and supplementary materials. The full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (odd/even with certain vs uncertain trials), includes within-task contrasts (Uncertain > Certain), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics (random-effects 1-sample and between-group t-tests; FWE-corrected maps and coordinate tables). The paper includes methods, results, and discussion describing whole-brain activation and task contrasts, meeting the meta-analysis requirements for ambiguous decision-making studies. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure wins and lotteries) while scanned. The paper reports within-task contrasts (presence vs absence of advice; parametric modulators for offer magnitude and certainty equivalents indexing safe vs risky valuation) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level corrected t-maps, reported coordinates and brain maps). Participants include adolescents and adults (healthy), and results are presented in main text and supplementary materials. Thus it meets all inclusion requirements for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney image categorization). The authors conducted EEG-informed whole-brain GLM fMRI analyses with condition comparisons (objects vs. scrambled/inverted faces) and direct contrasts (HF>LF, LF>HF) and report group-level, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and a table of peak coordinates (Table 1). Thus it includes fMRI during a perceptual decision task (I4), contains condition contrasts suitable for perceptual-DM (I5), provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation maps (I6), uses an eligible participant group (I7), and reports coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This study reports fMRI during a sentence–picture verification task (a semantic/verification decision), not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The reported voxelwise SPM contrasts shown in the paper are task > fixation (implicit baseline) rather than condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts required by the review. Therefore it fails the content inclusion requirements for decision-making type and uses baseline contrasts excluded by the review.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (50/50 monetary gambles), meeting the review topic. The study reports within-task contrasts (gain > loss and neural loss aversion parametric contrasts) and performs group-level random-effects SPM8 analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results reported as MNI coordinates and tables. Both within-group (shared gain>loss activations across groups) and between-group NLA contrasts are presented. The task is a risky DM paradigm, not a baseline-only contrast, and whole-brain maps (reported via coordinate tables and figures) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports combined fMRI and PET during a probabilistic reversal learning task and focuses on reward prediction error (RPE) signals. While it provides a voxelwise whole-brain (SPM) analysis with results reported (ventral striatum) and includes human participants (controls and patients) — satisfying I6 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I7 (participant groups acceptable) and I8 (results clearly described) — it does not meet the review’s task definitions. The task is a reversal learning/reinforcement-learning paradigm rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Crucially, the paper does not report contrasts of the form required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy); the main fMRI regressor is a parametric RPE modulator rather than an uncertainty/risk/perceptual difficulty contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task not in risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5. Exclusion IDs met: E5.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic passive-avoidance task (70% reward/punishment contingencies) that involves decision-making under uncertainty (risky decision-making). The study models decision-phase (approach vs avoid) and feedback-phase (reward/punishment) with parametric modulators (expected value and prediction error), and reports both ROI and whole-brain group-level (voxelwise) analyses (whole-brain results reported in Table 4 and main-effect analyses within the nonmaltreated group). Within-task condition contrasts (approach vs avoidance; reward vs punishment feedback; EV/PE-modulated responses) are present, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Participants are human children (age 10–15), an acceptable participant group. The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is an instruction-based learning/outcome-integration paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain contrast maps were computed), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described). Inclusion not met: I4 (the task is not a decision-making task under risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty), I5 (no appropriate decision-making contrast such as ambiguous > non-ambiguous or risky > safe was reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study used an intertemporal delay discounting task (choices between smaller-sooner and larger-later rewards), which is explicitly excluded by criterion E5 (delay discounting/intertemporal choice is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The full text reports within-task contrasts versus an active control (SS vs CON; LL vs CON), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and participant details, so it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, and I8 but fails I4 (task type). Full text appears complete. Exclusion: E5.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reported coordinates, but it does not report any of the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, or hard > easy). The reported fMRI contrasts are feedback-related (negative vs. positive feedback) and parametric prediction-error correlations, rather than contrasts that directly compare decision conditions (risk vs. safety or high vs. low ambiguity/difficulty). Therefore criterion I5 is not met, although I4, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered and the full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment with 30 human subjects performing a sequential investment task involving risk (I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results: parametric modulation by model-derived TD errors (outcome phase) and Q-values (choice phase), with cluster-corrected whole-brain statistics and reported peak coordinates (satisfies I6 and I8). The analyses constitute task-related contrasts (parametric modulators tested against zero), providing condition/task-related whole-brain contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (I5). Participants are healthy adults (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and not a non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete with methods, results (behavioral and fMRI), and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given these points, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making and should be included.

Excluded because the task is social/moral decision-making (truth-telling under asymmetric information) rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual; it is social/moral). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as required), I5 (no contrast matching the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts — the main contrast is true advice > false advice, a social honesty contrast rather than risky>safe or ambiguity contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study uses an fMRI trust game (human vs computer counterparts) that is a social decision-making task focused on betrayal aversion. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 explicitly excludes moral or social decision-making tasks. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM results and contrasts that include a risky > safe style comparison (trusting > not trusting) and provides coordinate tables, the task is fundamentally social/trust-based rather than the non-social risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making targeted by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails the inclusion requirement about task domain (I4) and must be excluded under E5.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with three manipulated error-rate conditions (20%, 50%, 80%). The main contrasts compare error-rate conditions (e.g., 20% vs 80%), meeting the requirement for a within-task decision-making contrast (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-corrected results are reported (voxelwise thresholding, cluster size, Talairach labels; Table 3, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are appropriate per inclusion criteria, and whole-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis scope of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and should be included.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). This is a value-based food vs. nonfood purchasing task (BDM auction) and thus falls outside the meta-analysis domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported with second-level GLMs and coordinate tables/figures), I7 (human healthy participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (the reported contrasts compare food vs nonfood valuation and sleep states rather than the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms required by the review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study that used a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with contrasts comparing decision > no-decision and risky > safe. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (SPM2) with FWE-corrected maps reported and ANCOVA group comparisons. Participant groups (controls, substance-dependent, substance-dependent with gambling) are acceptable. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a decision task involving explicit probabilistic outcomes (risk) while deciding whether to transfer a point (altruistic/helping under risk). The paper reports within-task contrasts and factorial comparisons (no self-risk vs high self-risk; low vs high other-need), parametric modulators of self-risk and other-need, and group-level whole-brain GLM results (voxelwise thresholds and cluster FWE correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Although the paradigm has a social/altruistic element, the decision variable is explicit probabilistic risk and thus fits the risky decision-making category. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Exclusion: E5 — the task is moral/social decision-making, which is explicitly excluded (not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group acceptable—healthy children/adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no fMRI of a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (contrasts reported are moral > nonsocial baseline rather than one of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms), I6 (uncertain whether a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task map is reported because full text is incomplete). Because E5 is met, the study is excluded.

This study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (exclusion E5). It instead examines statistical learning and prediction of symbolic sequences (prediction task), and though it contrasts structured vs. random sequences, the task is a learning/prediction paradigm rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. The paper also emphasizes ICA-based component and connectivity analyses and reports task effects as component β changes rather than providing a standard group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrast map; thus it effectively reports component/ connectivity results without the required voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps, fitting exclusion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (there is a contrast between two task conditions: structured vs. random), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (spatial maps/peak coordinates are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm), I6 (no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map appropriate for the meta-analysis). Therefore the study should be excluded.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I4. Although it is an fMRI study with a within-task contrast against an active control (PCLT > PMCT; meets I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (meets I6), involves human participants (meets I7), and provides whole-brain results described in the text (meets I8), the task used (Probabilistic Category Learning Task / Weather Prediction Task) is a category-learning feedback task and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports event-related fMRI collected while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (coherent motion discrimination), satisfying I4. The experiment manipulated perceptual difficulty (multiple coherence levels and two durations), providing within-task contrasts appropriate for perceptual-DM (e.g. low coherence vs high coherence, short vs long duration), satisfying I5. The paper describes group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses in addition to ROI analyses (group analysis results and thresholds are reported), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups (ASD and matched controls, ages 15–27) are acceptable under the review’s participant inclusion rules, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: the study does not rely solely on task>rest contrasts, is fMRI (not PET), reports task activation analyses rather than only ROI/connectivity results, and provides within-group effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task, with event-related parametric modulators indexing trial-by-trial risk/reward (e.g., Inflate*p(Explode), Success*p(Explode)). Analyses were performed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise statistics (SPM5) and report whole-brain clusters/tables linking task contrasts to behavior and substance use outcomes. The study therefore provides within-task condition contrasts (parametric high-risk vs low-risk modulation), whole-brain task activation maps, and involves a clinical human sample; results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content. On this basis the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. It is appropriate to include in the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a probabilistic (stochastic) classification task (weather prediction task) — a decision-making task under uncertainty (ambiguous/probabilistic). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects, FDR-corrected) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster tables. It contains at least one task-versus-active-control contrast (WPT > control task during presentation and feedback periods) and within-task contrasts relevant to uncertainty (high > low predictive value). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task under uncertainty), I5 (task > control and within-task contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that directly examines ambiguous decision-making (internal vs external subjective color choices) with within-task contrasts (ISD vs ESD, ISD vs EVD, ESD vs EVD). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM2, FDR-corrected voxelwise results, tables/figures), and contrasts are against an active veridical control (EVD) rather than rest. The paradigm therefore meets criteria for ambiguous decision-making, provides task-versus-task and ambiguous-versus-control contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting-state/connectivity-only.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (model-based prediction-error regressors) and includes eligible participant groups, the experimental task is a probabilistic reversal-learning reinforcement task focused on reward prediction errors rather than explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review.
