The paper does not present any of the required decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (task is not one of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast). It does satisfy I6 (whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (results clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (category judgments based on perceptual features) that manipulates uncertainty. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Far > Flanking, Flanking > Far, Training > Far) and parametric contrasts (distance from decision bound, distance from prototype), satisfying the requirement for decision-making condition comparisons. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs conducted with SPM8 and corrected for multiple comparisons; results are reported as statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Participants are healthy undergraduates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts only vs implicit baseline). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (mixed gambles) and includes healthy participants, but it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate tables. The analyses are ROI-based univariate regressions and PPI/DCM effective connectivity across predefined ROIs. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results and is effectively an ROI/connectivity-only report.
(a) Exclusion IDs met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E7 (reports effective/seed-based connectivity without reporting a whole-brain task activation map). 
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I7 (healthy participants). 
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no explicit admitted form contrast such as risky>safe or similar categorical decision-making contrast reported as voxelwise map), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables). 
Full text completeness: fulltext appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given E6/E7, exclude from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 applies: the fMRI contrast of interest reported is decision > fixation (task > rest/fixation), and the paper does not report a condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast (e.g., risky>safe). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — modified Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mapping was performed via MEPM), I7 (participant groups acceptable — substance-dependent and controls), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-vs-decision or task-vs-active-control contrast; the primary reported contrast is against fixation). Because E3 excludes studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline/rest/fixation, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite having whole-brain analyses. Full text appears complete and was used for screening.

This fMRI study used human participants performing a perceptual task (2IFC orientation detection) and healthy subjects, so inclusion criteria I4 and I7 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report any eligible decision-making contrast (e.g., hard>easy or perceptual task>control) for voxelwise task activation — the main fMRI analyses focus on MVPA/ROI-based decoding of spontaneous (rest) reactivation and retinotopically defined ROI results rather than condition-versus-condition task contrasts (I5 not met). Crucially, the study does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map; analyses are ROI-based (retinotopic and anatomical ROIs) and MVPA, so I6 is not met and exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results) applies. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (visual object categorization) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; degraded > intact; interactions of congruency and sensory reliability) and trial-specific RT regressors. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported (voxelwise results with cluster correction). Participants were healthy human volunteers. Results and contrasts are reported in the main text and tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion: E6 (only ROI-masked/striatum analyses reported; no whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise group-level task activation maps provided). Included criteria met: I4 (fMRI collected during a probabilistic loss-learning decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts/model-based contrasts for positive vs negative prediction errors and C− vs C+ drug-state contrasts), I7 (participant group acceptable—clinical substance-using sample), I8 (whole-brain-style results and coordinates/cluster statistics are described in the text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain, unmasked group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps; analyses were masked to the striatum and therefore constitute ROI-restricted results). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reinforcement learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (satisfying I4, I6, I7, and I8). However, it does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts comparing two decision-making conditions as specified in I5 (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty, risky > safe, hard > easy). The imaging results focus on parametric learning-related effects, stimulus vs feedback epochs, and between-group differences rather than explicit within-task contrasts between uncertainty/risk levels; therefore the study’s reported task activations appear to be contrasts against baseline/epochs and group comparisons rather than the condition-versus-condition contrasts required. This places the study into exclusion under E3 (only decision-making contrasts against implicit baseline/task epochs rather than condition-vs-condition contrasts) and fails I5. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E3.

This is a 3T fMRI study with human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) while inside the scanner. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing biased versus neutral cue conditions (bias vs neutral), conduct group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FLAME (cluster-corrected maps and conjunction analyses), and report whole-brain results in text/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts: bias vs neutral), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (human participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI scan during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) in human adolescents (I4). It includes explicit condition contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk choices (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (3×2×3 ANOVA) reported in the results and tables (I6). Participant groups (adolescents with depression/suicide attempt and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), the modality is fMRI (not PET), the task is a risky decision-making task (not excluded types), whole-brain results (not only ROI or connectivity) are reported, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an explicit audio-visual associative learning task that required trial-by-trial categorical predictions (a perceptual decision about visual stimulus category). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected) for task-related parametric modulators, including precision-weighted prediction errors and measures related to expected uncertainty (ε3/ψ3), which correspond to contrasts of high vs. low uncertainty/conditional probability (ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Results are reported in the main text with whole-brain maps and ROI-corrected analyses. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task parametric contrasts mapping to high vs low uncertainty/conditional probability), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a gambling task that manipulates risk levels (high- vs low-risk choices) and analyzes outcomes. The methods describe event-related fMRI, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses and report group- and risk-level contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk for positive outcomes; group×risk interactions). Results include whole-brain coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. Participant sample (healthy first-degree relatives and controls) is acceptable per the review scope. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making; relevant decision contrasts; whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps; acceptable participant group; clear reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with within-task contrasts (bad deck > good deck; framed vs control risk effects). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps and peak coordinates), and results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates. Participant groups include substance-dependent and non-substance-dependent individuals (eligible per I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI/connectivity, not task>rest only, includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study used human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (detecting short vs long digit sequences with implicit cues) manipulating uncertainty; it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing conditions (e.g., high vs low uncertainty checkpoints) and prediction-error contrasts (TERM>EXT, CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW), with thresholding and cluster correction. Behavioral and fMRI methods, results and discussion are present in full text. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task of perceptual nature), I5 (condition contrasts such as CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW, TERM>EXT), I6 (group whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria met: E3-E9 not applicable. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examined perceptual decisions about grating orientation and used fMRI during task performance (meets I4). However, the reported analyses focus on ROI-based MVPA and regressions within retinotopically-defined visual areas (V1–V3) and do not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or standard task contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low-coherence>high-coherence) required by the meta-analysis. The paper therefore fails to meet I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast reported) and I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task maps); because only ROI analyses are reported with no whole-brain results, it falls under exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that manipulated reward probability/uncertainty (slot machines A–D) during task performance and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Delay Slot_B > Delay Slot_A: high uncertainty > lower uncertainty). Group-level whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Contrasts correspond to ambiguous/risky decision-making comparisons (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. While it uses fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (I6) and includes a healthy participant sample (I7), and presents whole-brain results/coordinates in text (I8), the critical decision-making manipulation (valence ratings of surprised faces) was performed outside the scanner. In the MRI session participants freely viewed faces (passive viewing) and performed an emotion regulation task (reappraise vs maintain), which is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast comparing decision conditions or task vs control) are not satisfied. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study’s in-scanner tasks are not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study (Experiment 4) in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (accept/reject lotteries). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., gain > loss; accept > reject) and parametric contrasts for risk (variance) and EV, and tests interactions—i.e., condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 results with cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinates/tables of activations are provided. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (condition contrasts such as gain>loss, risk parametric effects), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline-only). Full text is complete. Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making paradigm, with participants scanned during task performance. The analyses include within-task, parametrically-modulated contrasts (inflation choice * P(explode); successful inflation * P(explode)) that constitute condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts, and second-level, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reporting peak coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which adolescents performed a risky decision-making lottery choice task during scanning. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses relating a parametric measure of risk (coefficient of variation; high-risk > low-risk contrast via parametric modulation) to BOLD responses, with cluster-level FWE correction. Results (whole-brain and ROI eigenvariates) are described in the text and supplements. Participants are a human sample (adolescents). Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This study used event-related fMRI of probabilistic reversal learning in Parkinson's patients, focusing on feedback-related and reversal-related activations (e.g., final reversal errors > correct responses). Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), includes a clinical participant group (I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/figures/tables (I8), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. The experimental contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses; nonswitch errors vs correct responses) index reversal-learning and feedback processing rather than formal risky/ambiguous choice contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the meta-analysis definitions. Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines risky decision making using a framing task (sure vs gamble under gain/loss frames) with healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., the framing-effect interaction: (Gsure + Lgamble) − (Ggamble + Lsure) and its reverse), and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests, whole-brain regression, cluster correction, and tables of activations). Behavioral and imaging results, methods, and discussion are present in the provided full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and activation results are presented in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline, not PET, task is a risky decision-making paradigm, whole-brain results are reported, and it is an empirical report). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (BART) (I4); it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Choose Inflate vs. Choose Win; Outcome Inflate vs. Outcome Explode) suitable for risky-DM contrasts (I5); analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level with cluster correction and reported in tables/figures (I6, I8); participant groups (high-risk and healthy youth, ages 10–14) are acceptable (I7). The task is a canonical risky-DM paradigm and contrasts are not against implicit baseline, results are not ROI-only or PET, and whole-text methods, results and figures are present, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion (E5, E6) — This is an fMRI study of category learning (rule-plus-exception) and does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (E5). The imaging analysis is focused on high-resolution, anatomically defined MTL and striatal ROIs rather than reporting unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps, so it reports ROI-restricted results with no qualifying whole-brain task maps (E6). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (contrasts are exception vs rule-following in a category-learning task, not the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete and was evaluated in full.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a probabilistic (uncertain) two-step decision task with monetary outcomes (decision-making under risk/uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and presents task-related contrasts/parametric modulators comparing neural responses as a function of prediction-error magnitude (high vs low SPE/RPE) and direct contrasts (e.g., SPE vs abs(RPE)). These are within-task, condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts tied to uncertainty and hence relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures. Participants are healthy humans. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This fMRI study had healthy human participants performing a dual-choice card gambling task that manipulated risk (high-risk vs low-risk) and used a parametric regressor for chosen risk. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported (SPM8) with FWE correction and whole-brain results (and ROI-constrained results) presented in tables and figures. The reported contrasts include risk-related activation scaling with risk magnitude (equivalent to high-risk > low-risk). The task and contrasts align with the review objective (risky decision-making). Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study in human adults implementing a perceptual decision-making task (nonsymbolic numerosity comparison) with an active, matched control task (brightness comparison). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA and parametric contrasts (cluster-corrected), and reports task > control and task-by-difficulty interaction effects identifying rIFG. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This fMRI study directly examines perceptual decision-making: participants made forced-choice /aba/ vs /ada/ judgments of ambiguous speech (perceptual DM). The authors ran GLMs labeling trials by participant percept (/aba/ vs /ada/) and report group-level whole-brain functional contrast maps (post-test trials > baseline; exposure blocks > baseline) and a group PPI map; thus task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise/surface analyses were performed even though the univariate /aba/ vs /ada/ contrast yielded no significant clusters. Multivariate decoding was additionally applied within STC. The design includes within-task comparisons of decision outcomes (perceptual labels), meeting the requirement for a decision-related contrast. Participants are healthy human adults. Results are reported in full-text figures and analyses. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task decision contrast: /aba/ vs /ada/ perceptions), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (human participant group qualifies), and I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study investigates social cooperation games (prisoner’s dilemma vs stag hunt) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social/moral decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I7 (human participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task per review definitions) and I5 (contrast is PD vs SH, not an accepted risky/ambiguity/perceptual contrast such as “risky>safe” or “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making that reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (high-risk vs low-risk; high-risk vs equal-risk; risk/reward vs control) in an adolescent sample, so it meets I4 (fMRI), I5 (decision-making contrasts), and I7 (eligible participant groups). However, the paper only reports ROI-constrained voxelwise tests (small-volume correction within pre-specified prefrontal ROIs) and presents ROI-based activations/coordinates rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Although the authors state that activations were collected brain-wide, all reported statistical tests and inference are restricted to a priori ROIs (SVC), and no whole-brain, unmasked group statistical maps or whole-brain voxelwise results are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic guessing task involving monetary rewards and penalties (risky decision-making), and reports contrasts comparing high- vs low-loss probability during number presentation and loss > win outcomes (meets I4 and I5). Participant groups (MDD and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). However, the MRI acquisition was limited to 23 oblique slices centered on the epithalamus (not whole-brain), and all group-level statistical analyses were conducted on beta coefficients averaged within manually defined habenula ROIs; the paper does not report unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore the study fails the whole-brain requirement (I6) and reports only ROI analyses (violating E6), so it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reward-learning task (Salience Attribution Test) that manipulates reward probability (high vs low) and includes ambiguous 50% probability conditions. It reports within-task condition contrasts (adaptive reward prediction: high-probability cues > low-probability cues; aberrant reward prediction: subjective high > low on task-irrelevant 50% cues) and random-effects, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates. The task therefore probes decision-making under risk/uncertainty and ambiguity, the contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), and whole-brain group maps are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI during passive viewing of food images (fattening vs. non-fattening) and an ad libitum eating paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and E6 (analyses are ROI-focused with no reported whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participants; healthy adult sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), I6 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; results are ROI-based). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of social/economic (Trust Game) decision-making focused on fairness and Machiavellianism. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Fair–Control, Unfair–Control) and provides voxelwise results, the task is social/moral/economic (trust/reciprocity) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — e.g., moral or social decision-making) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving simulation) with human adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe decisions (Go > Stop and Stop > Go) and feedback contrasts (Crash vs No-Crash). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxelwise threshold p = .001, cluster thresholds; tables of coordinates and figures provided). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain activation contrasts.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a perceptual phoneme categorization task (auditory post-tests) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects maps (satisfies I4, I6, I8). However, it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast as required by I5 (e.g., hard>easy, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or a task>active control). The primary whole-brain contrasts presented are audiovisual exposure blocks > baseline and a behaviorally weighted parametric modulation of exposure-block activation predicting later perception; no explicit within-scan contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., ambiguous vs less-ambiguous post-tests or hard vs easy perceptual trials) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E3 applies because the study’s main whole-brain task contrast is versus baseline and no appropriate condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast is provided. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion IDs met: E6 and E7. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — BART) and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy human participants across ages). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no clear reported contrast comparing decision-making conditions or task>control contrast in the paper text), I6 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented in the manuscript). Although the manuscript focused on fMRI data and reports ROI-based connectivity (GIMME) and extracted timepoints for “risky decisions,” the primary analyses are ROI-based effective/connectivity models rather than whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts. The paper does not provide clear, unmasked whole-brain task activation maps or within-task contrasts in the full text; therefore it meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E7 (only effective/connectivity analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete, but lacks the required whole-brain activation contrast for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescent females that implements a decision-making task with explicit risk manipulation (high-risk vs low-risk sexual decisions) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The manuscript includes within-task contrasts (high-risk > low-risk and Boys (high-low) vs. control conditions), reports whole-brain cluster results in tables and figures (voxel p<.001, cluster extent threshold), and provides full methods and results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which 24 healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (choose gamble vs guaranteed $10) while being scanned. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) showing neural correlates of decision risk (parametric modulation of gamble variance) and other decision variables. The key contrast is a trial-by-trial parametric effect of risk (i.e., high-risk > low-risk type effect) at the time of decision, reported as whole-brain maps and peak coordinates (Tables S1, S3). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in whole-brain activation tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI Methods). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that measured BOLD responses while subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task under ambiguity (face emotion morph judgments). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing ambiguity levels (e.g., increasing ambiguity and decreasing ambiguity effects) and identify whole-brain group-level activations using SPM random-effects analyses. Thus the paper provides eligible ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (ambiguous > non-ambiguous and related contrasts) and whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E7 — the paper reports ICA-derived networks and component betas (a connectivity/ICA approach) and does not report a standard group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast required for coordinate-based activation meta-analysis. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — fMRI was collected while participants performed a perceptual decision-making (two-choice RT) task; I7 — participants are human healthy adults (young and older) (participant groups acceptable); I8 — MNI coordinates for ICA component maxima are reported. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — no reported contrast of decision-making conditions (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high, or task>active control); the paper averaged across verbal and numerical blocks rather than presenting within-task condition contrasts; I6 — no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast map (e.g., task>control or condition>condition) is provided. Because I5 and I6 are required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This study conducted 3T fMRI while participants performed two-arm bandit decision-making tasks with probabilistic rewards and changing reward probabilities (social: faces smiling; non-social: houses open/locked). The fMRI analyses modeled volatility (uncertainty), prediction errors, and value expectation and tested whole-brain voxelwise encodings, reporting cluster coordinates and t-values (group-level whole-brain results). Thus it satisfies: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (parametric contrasts/analyses of uncertainty/volatility and decision-related computations consistent with ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, does not report only ROI or connectivity, and includes within-task computational modulators rather than only task>rest contrasts. Although one task was social, a non-social bandit was also acquired and modeled, and volatility/uncertainty-related regressors map onto ambiguous/risky DM constructs. Therefore include.

This is an event-related fMRI study (3T) in healthy human participants performing a game-theory-based risky decision task (iterated game of Chicken) involving risky/aggressive vs safe/reconciliatory choices. The design included within-subject contrasts (selection: risky vs safe) and opponent contrasts (human > computer), and a 2×2 factorial analysis; group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain FDR-corrected results and tables/figures). Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and task involves risky decision-making rather than purely social/no-uncertainty paradigms). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied.

The study used fMRI during a probability-discounting (risky decision-making) task and reported probability vs certain condition comparisons in behavioral and ICA-based imaging analyses, and participants meet acceptable groups. However, the imaging results are reported via independent component analysis (component spatial maps and component-level beta weights) rather than as a group-level, voxelwise task activation contrast (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/voxelwise contrasts such as probability>certainty are presented). This means it fails inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps) and falls under exclusion E7 (reports ICA/task-based network analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of reinforcement-based decision making using a probabilistic Paper-Scissors-Rock task that manipulates uncertainty across trials. The authors report within-task contrasts (early trials vs late trials reflecting higher vs lower uncertainty) and group-by-decision-time interactions. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (LME across all voxels with cluster correction) and results (and coordinates) are reported in text, figures, and supplements. Participants include occasional stimulant users and controls (eligible participant groups). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task with uncertainty/risk), I5 (within-task contrast comparing decision conditions: early>late / late>early), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task manipulating reward probabilities (HP 90% vs LP 75%), i.e., decision-making under uncertainty. The paper includes within-task and between-condition (HP vs LP) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., REVERR − ALLPOS within conditions and paired t tests comparing HP vs LP; parametric prediction-error regressors and HP–LP comparisons). These contrasts directly map onto an ambiguity/uncertainty comparison (high uncertainty [LP] vs low uncertainty [HP]) and therefore satisfy the meta-analysis contrast requirements. Whole-brain results are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participants are healthy human volunteers. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task outside risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM, baseline-only contrasts) apply.

This is a prospective fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making paradigm (Wheel of Fortune) with explicit probabilities. It reports within-task contrasts comparing high vs moderate and high/moderate vs equal risk/reward conditions and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons, with results described in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, scan acquisition, preprocessing, group analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used a delay-discounting (intertemporal) task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task, therefore failing the primary domain requirement for inclusion (exclusion E5). Additionally, the reported analyses focus on region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study contains within-task contrasts, e.g., immediate 'Today' trials vs. other decisions) and I7 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I6 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group activation map reported). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Given E5 (task domain) alone is sufficient for exclusion, the paper should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning (gambling-like) task but the reported contrasts are reward > punishment, punishment > reward, and final reversal error > baseline. None of the contrasts correspond to the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) required by inclusion criterion I5. The paper does provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates/tables, and it clearly describes the task and methods. However, because it lacks an eligible decision-making contrast quantifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, it does not meet I5 and is therefore excluded.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task analyses of a social learning/advice-taking task (satisfies I4, I6, I7, I8). However, the task centers on social decision-making (inferring adviser fidelity and integrating social advice with probabilistic cues) rather than a pure risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as defined by the meta-analysis. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 disallows studies whose decision-making task is social (e.g., social learning, advice/gambling framed by social motives). Furthermore, the reported contrasts are model-based social prediction errors and adviser-fidelity/integration effects rather than the domain-specific contrasts required for inclusion (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore I5 (required contrast type for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not met and E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I6) and tests uncertainty-related contrasts (e.g., variance/inverted-U; consistent with “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”) and thus meets I5, and the participant sample is acceptable (I7) and results are clearly reported (I8), the scanned task was a passive conditioning/imperative task (participants pressed a button indicating stimulus quadrant) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI. The authors explicitly state they used conditioning “to study the processing of economic parameters independent of choice.” Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (task must be a decision-making task performed during fMRI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

Full text is complete. This study used fMRI during a number-selection (stimulus–stimulus association and selection-conflict) task and reports group-level, whole-brain activation maps and within-task contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy adults and patient sample), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguity/uncertainty, or canonical perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review — it probes associative learning and selection/conflict rather than risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty), I5 (contrasts do not correspond to the review’s accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore exclude because the experimental paradigm does not match the meta-analysis target decision-making domains (risky, ambiguous, perceptual).

This is an fMRI study in humans that manipulated sexual risk (high vs low) while participants made decisions about likelihood of having sex, constituting a risky decision-making task. The study reports a within-task contrast comparing risk conditions (low > high), performs a group-level whole-brain SPM analysis with voxelwise results and Talairach coordinates, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Participants are healthy adult women. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during a risky decision-making task, (I5) at least one decision-condition contrast (high vs low risk), (I6) whole-brain group-level statistical maps reported, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) whole-brain results reported in text/tables. The full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, not non-empirical). The contrast direction (low>high) still represents a valid within-task risk condition comparison and is eligible for inclusion.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a decision-making task that involves risk (choice to take a challenge with probabilistic shock) and a perceptual discrimination challenge (vowel vs consonant). It includes within-task condition contrasts (Discouragement vs Control; Discouragement-successful > Control-successful) at the group random-effects level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported MNI coordinates and cluster corrections. Results include activation maps (insula, striatum) and psychophysiological interaction analyses, but critically also GLM whole-brain activation contrasts. Participants are healthy adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (certainty-equivalent gambling), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and condition-vs-condition contrasts (low-probability vs high-probability; low-value vs high-value). The manuscript reports whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables and links activation differences (notably in ACC) to behavioral parameters (Prelec α). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) in which healthy human males made decisions in a risky decision task (Stag hunt) while being scanned. The authors computed subject-level Stag > Rabbit contrasts and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (two-sample t-tests) and report cluster coordinates (left dlPFC) and functional connectivity results. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during human risky decision-making), I5 (explicit Stag > Rabbit condition contrast analogous to risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (coordinates/tables and clear description). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and reports within-task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty/probabilistic outcomes (i.e., risky decision context). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted: RPE-related parametric modulators were tested with one-sample and two-sample t-tests and whole-brain cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results (RPE network) are reported. The paper does not rely solely on ROI analyses and includes within-group task effects in healthy controls and patient subgroups. Although the task is framed as reinforcement/reversal learning rather than explicitly labelled “risky” or “ambiguous,” the probabilistic (80/20) choice structure entails risk/uncertainty and qualifies under the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI with a naturalistic risky decision (landing in fog) and included an active control (ILS approach without decision), but the reported analyses focus on ROI/small-volume results (bilateral caudate and other ROIs) and do not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (decision > active control/task contrast), I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6. Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using a choice reaction-time task that manipulates uncertainty/entropy (high vs low entropy) during decision-making. It reports within-task contrasts (entropy/response-alternative and reversal contrasts), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM and single-trial analyses, and presents whole-brain results (maps/tables). Participant sample is healthy adults. The task contrasts include high- vs low-uncertainty comparisons consistent with ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study uses fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement learning task (60% vs 40% reward contingencies) and reports whole-brain RPE (reward prediction error) activation maps. However, it does not present any of the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty; or equivalent ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Instead, the reported contrasts focus on outcome-related RPE signals (win RPE, loss RPE) and emotional (versus neutral) modulations, not explicit risky-versus-safe or uncertainty-based choice contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrast form) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast for the meta). The full text is complete and provides whole-brain group maps, so other inclusion criteria (I4, I6, I7, I8) are met.

This fMRI study used human participants (n≈27) performing a perceptual categorization task with parametrically varied uncertainty (entropy levels 3, 7, 8.5 bits/dot), directly manipulating perceptual decision difficulty (hard > easy). The analyses include contrasts assessing increasing activation with categorization uncertainty (parametric modulation/high uncertainty > low uncertainty), training-related contrasts (untrained > trained), and feedback-valence contrasts. Imaging was whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction; results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Thus it meets: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts reflecting uncertainty/hard>easy), I6 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Social Context Decision Task) during scanning. The authors report within-task condition contrasts that compare risky versus neutral outcomes (e.g., Regret [risky negative outcome] > Disappointment [neutral negative outcome]) and other decision-related contrasts (Regret>Relief, Relief>Elation, Disappointment>Elation), which serve as condition-versus-condition task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise GLM results with clusters reported in the text/tables and ROI time series derived from significant whole-brain peaks. Participants are healthy human subjects (late adolescents and young adults). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic wheel-of-fortune task (risky decision-making). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts of decision task versus non-reward control trials (e.g., anticipation [AR1, AR2, AR3] > AnRn; outcome contrasts versus OnwRn), satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-control contrasts. The full text includes methods, results, and tables of coordinates and description of whole-brain findings, meeting whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of the Trust Game (risky social decision-making) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (GAME>CONTROL, INVESTOR>CONTROL, TRUSTEE>CONTROL) and coordinates/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, all reported neuroimaging results are between-group comparisons (high-Mach > low-Mach) of the task contrast, and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task main effect map (e.g., task>control within a single group or the overall sample). Therefore it falls under exclusion E8 (reports only between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

The study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. It uses the Monetary Incentive Delay task (reward anticipation/receipt) and a Probabilistic Selection (reinforcement learning) task, which probe reward processing and reinforcement learning rather than decisions under risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria requiring an fMRI task of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and the prespecified contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). The full text is complete and reports group-level fMRI ROI and PPI connectivity analyses, but these do not fulfill the required decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task type), I5 (required decision-making contrasts), I6 (whole-brain task-activation map for the decision-making contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making).

The paper reports an fMRI experiment (n=26) in which participants made choices between certain and risky monetary options, satisfying the risky decision-making domain. The authors performed group-level, voxelwise fMRI analyses (random-effects, voxel-wise threshold P<0.001, cluster-level small-volume correction) and report coordinates and parametric contrasts linking option/outcome-related signals (EVs, RPEs, CRs) to BOLD activity in ventral striatum and insula. These constitute within-task decision-making contrasts (e.g., gamble vs certain/parametric modulators related to risk and reward expectation) and provide whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which human participants performed a lottery task manipulating outcome uncertainty and expected value. It tests neural responses to uncertainty (OU) and includes contrasts/parametric tests equivalent to “high uncertainty > low uncertainty” during curiosity induction and condition comparisons at outcome (Curiosity Relief–Yes > Curiosity Relief–No). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables reported. Participants were healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous task), I5 (within-task contrasts reflecting uncertainty/risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task, a decision-making paradigm involving choices under probabilistic uncertainty (risk). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., lose-shift vs. win-stay; lose-stay vs. win-stay; lose-shift vs. lose-stay) that index decision processes and feedback-driven choice, satisfying the requirement for a contrast between decision-making conditions. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistics (Monte Carlo-corrected thresholds) and report whole-brain results and ROI correlations. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and controls) are acceptable per inclusion rules. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., task>rest only, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face-based yes/no decisions), satisfying the review’s focus on perceptual DM. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., switch vs. stay trials) and other condition-wise comparisons, and presents univariate GLM results (group-level t-maps/contrasts) and whole-brain analyses (figures and statistical maps described), meeting the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts and whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not a review. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-option lottery Selection task) with fMRI acquisition and group-level whole-brain analyses. Reported task contrasts include within-task decision contrasts such as riskier > surer, gains > losses, and choice-determined value contrasts, satisfying the required risky-DM contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates reported in tables/supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This document is a commentary/preview summarizing and discussing Juechems et al. (2017) and related literature, not an original empirical fMRI study. Exclusion criterion met: E9 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none (inclusion_criteria_applied = []). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no original fMRI scan reported on human participants performing a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no reported task contrasts from an original experiment), I6 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or results). Additionally, the provided full text lacks core empirical sections (methods/results), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This study used fMRI in human participants performing an odour detection task (a perceptual task) and reports group-level, voxelwise searchlight MVPA results with coordinates; participants were healthy and whole-brain results are reported. However, it does not include the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., perceptual hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control) nor any within-task contrasts comparing two decision-making conditions of interest. Instead, analyses focus on pre/post-conditioning changes, multivariate pattern classification and connectivity (PPI) related to associative learning and value, not contrasts of perceptual decision difficulty. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one qualifying decision-making contrast) is not met, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain fMRI results from a two-step sequential reinforcement-learning task and provides group-level voxelwise contrasts (model-based vs model-free prediction-error regressors) and full methods/results/discussion. However, the meta-analysis specifically targets risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. The two-step task is a model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning paradigm and does not constitute a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; therefore it fails the task-domain inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (does not report contrasts in the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual forms). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It uses fMRI during an olfactory intensity-rating task combined with a memory (cognitive load) manipulation. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (healthy adult participants qualify), and I8 (whole-brain results and cluster/coordinate information are described). Not met inclusion criteria: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI) and I5 (no decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete and sufficient to determine eligibility.

EXCLUDED because the study does not provide a qualifying decision-making contrast per the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5). Although this is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-choice perceptual discrimination (color) task (meets I4), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures (meets I6 and I8), and participants qualify (meets I7), the critical requirement I5 is not met: the reported contrasts examine temporal expectancy (good vs bad clock) and accessory (vibration) effects, and task>rest contrasts, but do not include perceptual difficulty or perceptual decision contrasts of the accepted forms (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>active control) nor ambiguity/risk contrasts (high uncertainty>low uncertainty in the decision dimension). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study (BART during scan) meets I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported) and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/text). However, it does not present a qualifying condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast as required by I5. The reported analyses appear to be condition > implicit baseline contrasts (e.g., pumps/cash-outs modeled against the implicit baseline) and age regressions on these condition maps; there is no clear “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “pump > cash-out”, or other within-task risky-vs-safe or task-vs-control contrast presented. Because the study’s decision-making contrasts are only against an implicit baseline, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (rating risk of physical activities) manipulating likelihood and severity. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; high-harm > low-harm; Risk x Format interactions) rather than only task>baseline. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (the fMRI task is an emotional go/no-go impulse-control paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E7 (the primary reported analyses are pseudo-resting-state/functional connectivity and multivariate prediction of “brain age,” not whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation maps or task contrasts). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (the participant group is within eligible populations). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no fMRI performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no reported contrasts of the form risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; the paper does not report decision-making task-versus-control-task contrasts relevant to the review), and I6 (the target analyses are connectivity/prediction rather than group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these points, the study does not meet the required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is primarily moral/social decision-making (allocating financial harm/help to a charity vs self), which the meta-analysis explicitly excludes. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI results reported with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinates), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is framed as social/moral decisions rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the review), and I5 (no contrast matching the admissible risk/ambiguity/perceptual forms such as "risky > safe" or "high uncertainty > low uncertainty"; condition contrasts focus on self vs charity and gain vs loss rather than risk vs safe or ambiguity contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion summary: E5 applies — the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm but a visuomotor/sequence-statistics finger-tapping task assessing entropy and surprise in stimulus/action sequences. Included criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses were conducted and reported), I7 (healthy adult participants were tested), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and supplementary material). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (there is no eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrast of the forms required by the review; the main contrast is choice vs specified action related to sequence regularity, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human healthy adults using a risky decision-making task (the Cups task) with immediate feedback. It reports task contrasts of interest (e.g., Risky > Safe and Win > Loss), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based correction, and provides coordinates and figures for significant activations. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (relevant decision-making contrasts such as risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets several inclusion criteria for the review (it used fMRI during a decision-making reward/number-guessing task [I4]; it reports decision-making versus active control contrasts (Win-Control, Loss-Control) [I5]; the participant sample (youth including clinical and healthy groups) is acceptable [I7]; results/coordinates and ROI results are clearly reported in the text and figures [I8]). However, the group-level statistical testing was conducted and reported within a predefined reward-circuitry ROI (reward circuitry mask) rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. The manuscript thresholds Z-statistic images within the ROI mask (small-volume/restricted search), and no unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps are reported. This violates the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and therefore falls under exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy humans (n=30) using a perceptual decision-making task (bistable motion) and presents within-task contrasts (incoherent > coherent) comparing perceptual decision conditions. Group-level, whole-brain RFX-GLM voxelwise results, statistical maps, and coordinates are reported, and methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans performing a mirror-reading lexical decision task (mirror vs normal) that manipulates perceptual difficulty and measures task-evoked whole-brain activation. The key contrast (mirror > normal) compares two task conditions (perceptual-hard > perceptual-easy) and therefore qualifies as a perceptual decision-making contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with peak coordinates reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET study, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses functional MRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (I4), reports task contrasts comparing decision conditions including gamble > sure (choice regressor; I5), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects statistics and whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates (I6, I8), and includes an eligible participant group of healthy adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods (task, behavioral modeling, fMRI acquisition and GLM), results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging tables/coordinates), and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This study used fMRI and whole-brain group analyses of a probabilistic reversal-learning task (feedback: positive vs negative; loss/switch vs loss/stay), but it does not probe the meta-analysis’ target domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) nor report the specific decision-making contrasts required. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain maps were reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described). Inclusion not met: I4 (task is reversal learning/feedback-guided learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM paradigm as defined by the review), I5 (no accepted risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”; primary contrasts are reward vs. punishment and switch/stay). Exclusion applied: E5 (decision-making task is not one of risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM per the review criteria). Full text appears complete.

Only the article abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract it is clear this is an fMRI study in human participants performing a categorisation task of prosodic expressions (meets I4) and the authors report contrasts involving ambiguous versus typical tokens (consistent with an 'ambiguous > non-ambiguous' contrast, suggesting I5). Participant inclusion criteria are broad (I7) and results are described in the text (I8). However, the available content does not include the full methods or results needed to confirm that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported (I6) or to verify the exact contrasts and their masking/statistical thresholds. Because core article content (methods/results) is missing, I cannot confidently verify all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis were clearly triggered by the abstract alone. Therefore I exclude on the basis of incomplete full text preventing confirmation of required whole-brain, condition-vs-condition contrasts.

This fMRI study examines social approach/avoid judgment of facial expressions (social decision-making about ambiguous stimuli). Although it meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (I4: fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task; I5: contains a decision-making task versus an active control task contrast — social judgment > sex discrimination; I6: reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses; I7: uses an eligible participant group [healthy adults]; I8: whole-brain results are reported in text/figures), it must be excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E5. The task is explicitly social decision-making (approach/avoid), which the review’s exclusion criteria list as not qualifying (e.g., moral or social decision-making is excluded). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI during a perceptual task (texture discrimination) and reports whole-brain task-evoked activation, but it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast of the forms required (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, perceptual task > active control). The fMRI analyses derive and compare task-induced activation maps (averaged across conditions) and report group differences and pre/post session effects; the reported effects appear to be task > implicit baseline and between-group differences rather than a within-task condition contrast or task > active control contrast. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/task activity) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrast).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with decision-making under uncertainty (70% vs 30% reinforcement). It includes within-task condition contrasts (experienced outcome contrasts such as Gain vs Loss-avoidance and expected-value contrasts [Positive – Negative]) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported in figures/tables. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control groups (allowed). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during decision-making under probabilistic outcomes), I5 (within-task condition contrasts comparing decision conditions: experienced and expected valence contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task and reports whole-brain fMRI contrasts (e.g., final reversal errors vs perseverative errors; correct vs incorrect; perseverative vs probabilistic errors). However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (no risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy contrasts). Therefore it fails the key task-related inclusion criteria. Exclusion ID: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy, substance users), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast such as risky>safe or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task during scanning.
