The paper reports within-task contrasts that separate outcomes by risk level (e.g., aversive outcomes following low-, medium-, and high-risk choices), parametric risk-level analyses (linear effects across odds), and pharmacological challenge interactions; these constitute condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results (FWE-corrected clusters reported, peak MNI coordinates provided), and additional ROI and ASL checks are supplementary. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps.

The study reports task-based whole-brain fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (PRLT) that uses explicit probabilistic feedback (80:20), i.e. decision-making under uncertainty/risk, and includes an affectively neutral active baseline control task. The authors computed within-task contrasts (monetary gain vs baseline, monetary loss vs baseline, reversal vs baseline) and performed group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2, random effects) with whole-brain thresholding and tabulated/figured results. Participants include clinical and control groups. Thus the paper meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (experimental task > active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contrasts are against active control not implicit baseline; within-group task effects reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Jackpot play/pass with 33% vs 67% probabilities), includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices (Play > Pass and Gain/Loss > Pass) and contrasts between contexts (Social vs Monetary Play), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participants are human and eligible. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a spatial memory retrieval task in morphing virtual environments, not a canonical risky, ambiguous economic, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Although participants made memory-based placement choices in ambiguous contexts, the paper’s analyses focus on MVPA pattern similarity (sigmoidal vs linear models) and hippocampal remapping rather than standard decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous) or univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps appropriate for the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during task), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (reporting of coordinates/whole-brain results in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no standard contrast comparing decision conditions or task > control as required), I6 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps presented for the decision contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the meta-analysis entry criteria: it acquired fMRI while participants (adolescents) performed the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making) and reports a risky > safe (risky vs. safe) contrast. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise (SPM8) with correction and reported coordinate results. Participant groups (healthy and excess weight adolescents) are within eligible populations and results include within-group and between-group task activations and contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only) apply.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which participants performed explicit monetary decision-making tasks under risk (probability discounting and 50-50 gambles). Group-level, voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVAs and exploratory whole-brain analyses) are reported, with parametric regressors for subjective value, magnitude, and probability; results are presented in the main text and supplementary tables. The study thus (a) acquired fMRI during risky decision-making (I4), (b) reported within-task parametric contrasts relating neural activity to subjective value/potential gain/potential loss (acceptable forms of decision-related contrasts, satisfying I5), (c) conducted and reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I6) and provided results in text/tables (I8), and (d) included clinical and healthy participant groups (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to task>rest only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (phoneme categorization /ba/ vs /da/) during scanning; searchlight MVPA produced condition-vs-condition (binary) contrasts entered into group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (voxelwise p<0.001, cluster correction), with results reported in figures and corrected p-values. Thus the study meets I4 (perceptual DM), I5 (within-task condition contrast /ba/ vs /da/), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy participants included), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria E3–E9 apply. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants using a probabilistic monetary-incentive delay task that systematically manipulated outcome probability (20%, 50%, 80%) and magnitude. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high- versus low-probability anticipation (PRB: 80 vs 20%) and other decision-related contrasts, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach coordinates. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for (I4) an fMRI task involving probabilistic (risky) decision-related processing, (I5) at least one decision-related within-task contrast (high vs low probability), (I6) group-level whole-brain results, (I7) an acceptable participant group (healthy humans), and (I8) reporting of whole-brain results with coordinates and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participant sample), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s task-type inclusion requirements. Although it reports group-level whole-brain fMRI results (I6) and includes eligible participant groups (I7) and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I8), the experimental paradigm is a probabilistic social reinforcement learning task (social reward learning) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. The paper does not report contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) or within-task risk/ambiguity contrasts; instead analyses focus on reinforcement learning (trial-wise RPE parametric modulation) and social vs non-social feedback. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Included criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because its reported fMRI contrasts are condition-versus-baseline (e.g., wins > baseline, lose/shift > baseline) rather than condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts (violates E3). Additionally, the imaging analysis was performed using a region-of-interest approach with no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps reported (violates E6). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm that is not clearly one of the specified risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM tasks as operationalized by the review), I5 (no eligible decision-versus-decision or task-versus-control contrasts presented), I6 (no whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Overall confidence in this exclusion decision is high.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the fMRI task does not probe risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the scanned task was an attentional/conditioned-cue probe (CS+ vs CS−) and the decision-making task (delay discounting) was performed outside the scanner. Therefore this study does not address risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM and fails the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Exclusion ID met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted while participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy was reported for an in-scanner decision task). Given these mismatches, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dynamically adaptive motion prediction). The authors report within-task condition contrasts (errors with negative feedback vs correct trials with positive feedback), which reflect comparisons between decision-making conditions (errors correspond to more difficult/uncertain perceptual decisions), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (voxel-wise one-sample t tests, z-maps, tables/figures), and coordinates/activations are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study acquired BOLD data while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task, parametric contrasts across risk levels (i.e., activation associated with increasing pump/risk levels) and examines whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (within-group effects and group comparisons are described). Participants are human (healthy MBA students). Results are reported in the main text with methods, results, and discussion present (full text appears complete). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6) and also meets participant and reporting acceptability (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (BART) in adolescents with group-level whole-brain results and relevant ROIs, but it reports the main effect of risk decisions (pump events) relative to an implicit baseline. The paper does not present a condition-vs-condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe or pump > cash-out) nor a task > active control contrast. According to the review criteria, studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline must be excluded (E3). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion I5 (required condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded due to E3.

This is an fMRI study in humans that directly investigates perceptual decision-making using ambiguous and unambiguous trials, meeting the review scope. It reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (FWE-corrected results) and model-based parametric contrasts relating trial-by-trial prediction variables to BOLD activity. The design includes within-task contrasts and parametric modulators that assess perceptual decision processes (e.g., conditional probabilities, prediction errors) and separate modeling of ambiguous vs. unambiguous trials for ROI definitions, which fulfill the requirement for a decision-related contrast (ambiguous/perceptual decision conditions vs. others) rather than only task>baseline. Participants are healthy adults. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of human risky decision-making (choice between certain amount and gamble) with 21 healthy participants, meeting I4. The analyses include condition contrasts comparing risky versus non-risky choices and other task-based contrasts (e.g., risky > certain; amount-related contrasts), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level voxelwise GLMs and second-level one-sample t-tests with reported MNI coordinates and voxelwise inference (with Small Volume Correction applied to ROIs), indicating availability of whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or coordinate-based whole-brain results, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample are healthy adults, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only without whole-brain results, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion criteria met: E3. This study performed fMRI while participants completed a risky decision-making task (IGT) and provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps, but the reported within-task contrasts are task versus rest (implicit baseline) and the group comparisons are between FH+ and FH-; no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control decision-making contrasts (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'high-risk > low-risk', or 'task > control task') are reported. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I5 (no appropriate decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because E3 is met, study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study used an n-back working memory fMRI task (0-back vs 2-back) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Thus it does not meet I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) nor I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity contrasts, or hard>easy). The paper does report group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps and within-group results (satisfying I6) and includes relevant participant groups (I7) and clearly describes whole-brain results in the text (I8). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a monetary reward-learning task emphasizing reward prediction error (RPE) and connectivity (gPPI). However, it did not manipulate or contrast risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making conditions (no contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). The task and reported contrasts focus on RPE/RE/OE and seed-based connectivity; activation analyses were constrained to a reward-related mask rather than presenting an unmasked whole-brain task activation map relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement that the fMRI task be a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm (Exclusion E5). Met inclusion criteria: I7 (participant group acceptable) and I8 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). Not met: I4 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts), I6 (no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a qualifying decision-making contrast).

This study used fMRI to investigate visual pattern recognition learning (Igo puzzles) with participants instructed to passively view stimuli during scanning. Although whole-brain, group-level activation maps and contrasts (Igo vs non-Igo, Day-3 vs Day-1) are reported (meets I6 and I8) and the participant sample is acceptable (I7), the fMRI task was not a risky, ambiguous, or clearly defined perceptual decision-making task: subjects were instructed not to solve problems during scanning and the paradigm targets learning/recognition rather than an explicit perceptual decision contrast (hard>easy or low>high coherence). Therefore the key inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (a decision-making contrast) are not met. This study is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) (I4). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs safe decisions) and reports group-by-decision analyses (risky > safe / risky vs safe contrasts are analyzed) (I5). Second-level, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (AlphaSim) are performed and reported (I6). Participant groups include substance-using and comparison subjects, which are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and the report includes within-task condition contrasts rather than only between-group effects. The provided full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (face same/different discrimination with morphed stimuli). It reports within-task contrasts (subjective ‘same’ vs ‘different’ and parametric modulation by morphing distance corresponding to perceptual difficulty/hard>easy comparisons), performed with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM) and reports coordinates/tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

Although this study used fMRI with human participants and included a perceptual judgment of acoustically ambiguous stimuli (word vs. pseudoword), it does not provide the required decision-making contrast specified by the review (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, hard > easy, or task > active control). The reported contrasts are between subjectively word- versus pseudoword-perceived trials (content-based lexical/phonological contrasts) rather than formal decision-making condition contrasts manipulating uncertainty or perceptual difficulty. The paper does report group-level, whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables, and participants were appropriate, but the critical inclusion criterion I5 (at least one acceptable decision-making contrast) is not met. Therefore it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this study used fMRI in human participants on a gambling task (risky context) and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts, it does not present a qualifying decision-making contrast as required (I5). The primary reported contrasts are outcome-based (wins > non-wins; near-miss > full-miss; interaction of near-miss by personal control) rather than contrasts comparing decision options by risk or ambiguity (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy). The selection-phase (participant-chosen vs computer-chosen) is not an explicit risky vs safe or ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrast. Therefore I5 is not met, so the study must be excluded. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a gambling/guessing task that manipulates reward probability and magnitude (risky decision making). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and corrected statistical maps, and includes contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., high vs low probability; gain > loss; EV+ vs EV− prediction/prediction-error contrasts). Thus it fulfills the review’s requirements for (i) fMRI during a risky DM task, (ii) condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making, (iii) whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and (iv) acceptable participant sample (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI results for a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the behavioral paradigm is a time-perception/interval estimation task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E7 (the neuroimaging data reported are resting-state seed-based connectivity analyses rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group is acceptable; healthy volunteers were tested). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan performed while subjects completed a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrast comparing decision-making conditions such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study used an fMRI cue-reactivity task (passive viewing of cocaine-related vs natural scene images) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps. However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task nor contrasts of decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups: substance users/controls), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is thus met, so the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study includes a probabilistic discounting (PD) task that is a risky decision-making paradigm (choices between sure €20 and probabilistic rewards), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (parametric subjective-value regressors) with coordinates and statistical maps. The PD analysis provides within-task contrasts (subjective value correlation for probabilistic options) that constitute a decision-making effect appropriate for risky-DM meta-analysis. The full text contains methods, results, and figures/tables documenting whole-brain results (with SVC reported but based on group-level voxelwise maps). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and it includes within-task task effects rather than only baseline contrasts. Although the paper also includes delay-discounting (an excluded task type), the presence of a qualifying risky (probability) task and whole-brain PD contrasts satisfies inclusion. Therefore include.

This fMRI study tested PD patients performing a probabilistic roulette task with explicit risk manipulations (0.25 vs 0.75 win probabilities and $1 vs $5 stakes), i.e., a risky decision-making paradigm. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses: (a) outcome-induced BOLD changes and (b) trial-by-trial parametric modulation by reward prediction error (RPE) values, entered into repeated-measures ANOVAs. The RPE parametric contrast and categorical analyses of negative vs positive RPE constitute within-task decision-making contrasts relevant to risky DM (not simple task>baseline only). Whole-brain results are reported and thresholded, and coordinates/tables are provided. Participants are a clinical sample (PD), which is allowed. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (observers reported perceived motion direction; satisfies I4), included condition comparisons involving coherence/ambiguity (0% ambiguous vs 50/100% unambiguous; satisfies I5), and tested healthy human participants (satisfies I7). However, the paper reports ROI-based multivoxel pattern classification results (V1–V4v, V3a, hMT+, IPS, FEF) rather than a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map or univariate whole-brain contrasts. It therefore does not provide the required whole-brain evidence (fails I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Accordingly, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a forced-choice categorization task (valence classification of faces) during scanning. The task constitutes a perceptual decision-making paradigm with manipulated difficulty via congruent vs. incongruent background colors; the primary reported contrasts are condition-versus-condition (e.g., incongruent > congruent) within emotional categories. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM2) voxelwise analyses are reported with tables of coordinates, conjunction and interaction analyses, and ROI/PSC follow-ups. Participants (n=20) are an eligible human sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9).

This study is excluded because the task is primarily social/vicarious reward prediction (self vs other empathy paradigm) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is social decision-making/motivated by empathy rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task). The study does meet several methodological inclusion requirements: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation with FWE-corrected results), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (reports coordinates/figures). However it does not meet I4 (the paradigm is not a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task—participants made expectedness judgments about observed/probabilistic outcomes rather than making risk/ambiguity or perceptual choice decisions) and I5 (it does not provide contrasts that map onto accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because its fMRI tasks are cue-reactivity and response-inhibition, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks (Exclusion E5). Additionally, the imaging analysis was restricted to an ROI mask rather than a whole-brain task activation map, meeting Exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group qualifies) and I8 (whole-brain results may be reported in tables/coordinates — the paper reports activation coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no eligible decision-making contrasts of the accepted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI during monetary incentive delay (MID) and a probabilistic reward (response-bias) task in nonsmokers, with whole-brain, group-level contrasts (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue; Loss Cue–Neutral Cue). However, neither task matches the review’s target decision-making domains. The MID probes anticipation of monetary gains/losses and simple RT performance rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (eg, risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). The probabilistic reward task is a reward-learning/perceptual discrimination with asymmetric reinforcement but the reported contrasts focus on response bias rather than accepted perceptual-DM contrasts (eg, hard>easy or low vs high coherence). Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5, despite meeting other criteria (whole-brain group maps present). Full text is complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy humans performing a monetary gambling task that manipulates risk. It includes within-task condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk wins > low-risk wins; a risk-choice contrast modeling linear increase with risk magnitude), satisfying the required risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain (SPM8 second-level ANOVAs) with reported whole-brain clusters and ROI-corrected results, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not only baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded DM types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the paper reports task activations rather than only connectivity or between-group-only contrasts. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This fMRI study used a visual food perception paradigm (Food > Non-Food) in healthy participants and reports group-level task effects. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the task is passive viewing with attention targets and tastiness ratings, not a risky/ambiguous choice or a perceptual decision manipulation (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level task-evoked analysis/second-level random-effects contrasts were generated and whole-brain effects are reported/supplemented), I7 (participant group acceptable: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported in text/figures/supplement). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Hence the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study is whole-brain and used tasks including a perceptual color-detection task, but it does not contain an eligible decision-making contrast as required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (healthy adult participants allowed), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 — the paper does not report an accepted decision-making contrast (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or perceptual hard>easy / perceptual task>control). The main contrasts are social/intention (Shared vs Parallel Intentions) and task attention (Intention vs Color), not perceptual difficulty or decision-making contrasts per the meta-analysis definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.
